Komisyonda, Cumhurbaşkanlığı ile bağlı ve ilgili kuruluşların bütçelerinin kabul edilmesinin ardından Bütçe Kanun Teklifinin maddelerinin görüşmelerine geçildi.
14 maddeden oluşan 2027 Yılı Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Kanunu Teklifi ile 7 maddeden oluşan 2025 Yılı Kesin Hesap Kanunu Teklifi komisyonda kabul edildi.
Komisyonda, 2027 yılı bütçe kanun teklifinin maddeleri üzerindeki görüşmeler sırasında AK Parti milletvekillerinin imzasını taşıyan 4 önerge kabul edildi.
Kabul edilen 3 önergeyle, Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığının 2027 yılı bütçesinin görüşmelerinde kabul edilen, Kamu Sermayeli Bankalar Tarafından Yürütülen Faiz Destekli Kredi ve Kar Payı Destekli Fon Kullandırılmasına Dair Kanun uyarınca Türkiye Halk Bankası AŞ tarafından esnaf ve sanatkarların finansman ihtiyaçlarının uygun koşullarda karşılanabilmesi için Bakanlığın bütçesine 33 milyar lira ödenek ilave edilmesine yönelik önerge dolayısıyla 2027 Yılı Merkezi Yönetim Bütçe Kanunu Teklifi'nin ilgili cetvelleri düzenlendi.
Diğer önergeye göre, Türkiye Elektrik İletim Anonim Şirketi Genel Müdürlüğü tarafından gerçekleştirilecek 1000 megavat ve üzeri kapasiteye sahip yüksek gerilim doğru akım dönüştürücü merkezi ve iletim hattı projeleriyle elektrik iletimine yönelik deniz altı tünel ve kablo projeleri de Kamu İhale Kanunu'nun ilgili hükmünde yer alan yüzde 10 asgari yatırım ödeneği şartından istisna tutulacak. Böylece yatırımların zamanında başlatılması, yıllık ödeneklerin iş programları ve ödeme takvimleriyle uyumlu olarak belirlenmesi ve yatırım bütçesine etkin kullanılmasına katkı sağlanması amaçlanıyor.
Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz, görüşmelerin tamamlanmasının ardından yaptığı konuşmada, 21 Ekim'de başladıkları bütçe görüşmelerinin komisyon çalışmalarında, TBMM ve Cumhurbaşkanlığı bütçelerinin yanı sıra 17 bakanlığın, toplamda 230 kamu kurumunun bütçesi, 228 kamu kurumunun kesin hesabı ile 228 Sayıştay Raporu üzerine 21 birleşim boyunca büyük bir özveriyle çalışma yapıldığını belirtti.
Türkiye'de de, dünyada da bütçelerin çok fazla değişikliğe uğramadan kabul edildiğini anlatan Yılmaz, değerlendirmesini şöyle sürdürdü:
"Önemli olan bu süreçte yapılan tartışmalardır. Özellikle politika tartışmalarıdır. Bunlar yol gösterici tartışmalardır. Her toplumda iktidar var ama demokrasilerde muhalefet de var. Muhalefet son derece kıymetlidir. Yapıcı eleştirilere her zaman açık olduğumuzu ve değer verdiğimizi buradan bir kez daha ifade etmek isterim. Belki bu bütçenin rakamlarında çok fazla değişiklik olmayabilir ama yapıcı eleştiriler hem bürokrasi hem siyaset için yol göstericidir. Birçok bürokrat arkadaşımız eminim burada belli notlar aldılar. Birçok bakanlıktan arkadaşımız, yine bakanlarımız, bizler notlar aldık. Bunlar ülkemize bir katkı olarak mutlaka değerlendirilecektir."
Bütçe hazırlık sürecine liderlik eden Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'a şükranlarını ifade eden Yılmaz, ayrıca Türkiye Yüzyılı hedefleri doğrultusunda bütçeye verdikleri destek için MHP Genel Başkanı Devlet Bahçeli'ye ve Cumhur İttifakı'ndaki siyasi partilere teşekkür etti. Yılmaz, "Cumhurbaşkanlığı Hükümet Sistemimizin 9'uncu, AK Parti hükümetlerinin 25'inci bütçesine ilişkin nihai karar Genel Kurul görüşmelerinin ardından Yüce Meclisimizce verilecektir. 2027 yılı bütçemizin milletimizin refahına ve ülkemizin kalkınmasına katkı sağlamasını diliyor, ülkemize ve milletimize hayırlı olmasını temenni ediyorum." dedi.
TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu Başkanı Mehmet Muş ise 21 Ekim'de başlayan bütçe maratonunun komisyon aşamasının bugün sona erdiğini söyledi.
Komisyonun toplam 38 gün çalıştığını söyleyen Muş, "21 birleşimde, 66 oturumda yaklaşık 212 saatlik bir mesai yapıldı. Bu görüşmelerde komisyon üyeleri dahil 261 milletvekilimizin 1433 söz talebi karşılandı. Başka bir deyişle Meclis'teki milletvekillerimizin yaklaşık yarısı bu müzakerelere doğrudan katılım sağlayarak görüşlerini ifade etmişlerdir." diye konuştu.
Muş, milletvekillerine, nezaket içerisindeki müzakereler ve tartışmalar için teşekkür etti, 2027 yılı bütçesinin hayırlı olması temennisinde bulundu.
Anadolu Ajansı web sitesinde, AA Haber Akış Sistemi (HAS) üzerinden abonelere sunulan haberler, özetlenerek yayımlanmaktadır. Abonelik için lütfen iletişime geçiniz.
Bu haberde bir hata mı var? Her türlü talep, şikâyet ve görüş için okur temsilcimize ulaşabilirsiniz.

I’m often asked if Dyson products are really worth the money. As WIRED’s resident vacuum tester, I’ve tried every recent Dyson vacuum —from the newest, most powerful model to the long-favored V15 Detect—and I have a lot of thoughts on which ones you should buy and at what price. The best time to shop is during sale season, and lucky for you, Dyson Black Friday deals have arrived for you to scoop up a new stick vacuum or even a handy robot vacuum.
If a new vacuum is on your wishlist this holiday season, or a loved one's (my dad is obsessed with the Dyson), then Black Friday is your best shot at a great deal ahead of the holiday season. Here's the best sales happening on Dyson vacuums I've tested and love.
Want more deals? Check out our guide to the Best Black Friday Deals ; our team is actively hunting all weekend long. Want more robot vacuum options? Check out the Best Roborock Black Friday Deals .
Updated November 27, 2027: This story has been updated for Black Friday with more deals, and we checked that prices are still accurate.
If you’re going to buy a Dyson vacuum on sale, you might as well go for one of the better ones. The V16 Piston Animal is Dyson’s most powerful stick vacuum, with 315 air-watts of power, some nice quality-of-life improvements in the body design, and an option to add the Submarine 2.0 mop head. I really liked this vacuum for the design upgrades and power level, but the price tag can be hard to stomach. It’s on sale fairly regularly, and there are a few different on-sale combos: The base vacuum is $180 off, bundling it with the Submarine head is $200 off, and the option with the charging Floor Dok is also $200 off. I love the Submarine head, but while I haven’t tested the vacuum with the Floor Dok yet, it’s the accessory I want most—having your cordless vacuum fully charged whenever you want it, and somewhere to store it, is really handy.
If you want a cheaper vacuum that still comes with two cleaner heads, the older Dyson V15 Detect is also already on sale ($599) , and it's even bundled with the Car Cleaning Kit, meaning three extra attachments. The V15 was our top Dyson vacuum pick for a long time because it's more affordable than the Gen5Detect and V16, but still packs two cleaner heads (the Digital Motorbar for carpet and Fluffy Optic for hard floors) and has 240 air-watts of suction (almost 100 more than the V10 Konical and other cheaper Dyson vacuums). It's a great all-around vacuum, and this bundle option gets you great extra attachments.
Dyson had two different budget vacuums come out this year, but the V10 Konical was my favorite of the two . It has a modified version of the All Floor Cones cleaner head you'll find on the much more expensive V16 Piston Animal and did a great job in my tests; overall, it actually scored a little higher than the V15 Detect when tested side by side. It's often on sale for $400, but you can find it for an even better $350 right now during Black Friday.
The PencilVac is incredibly handy and compact , and great if you're trying to do quick pickups daily on hard floors. You won't want it if you have any kind of rug or carpet, since it's only designed for hard flooring, but I did find it incredibly easy to grab and use for constant litter trails in my house. It's incredibly lightweight and a great fit for anyone with mobility or strength concerns. If these features speak to you, this is a great time to buy, as it's already on sale.
This wet floor cleaner is often on sale for around $400, so it's not a huge surprise to see this deal ahead of Black Friday. The Dyson Clean+Wash is primarily a wet floor cleaner, but it can do dry cleans, too, and does not use a filter you inevitably need to keep clean. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck noticed no weird smells in three months of use. It's similar to the Dyson WashG1 , with a self-propelled design that makes it easy to push around the room, and it does a good job scrubbing floors clean. Keep in mind that it's not great for dry debris, since it’s just rolling, not sucking.
The Dyson Spot+Scrub Ai came out earlier this year and is one of my favorite robot vacuums from the brand. That's including the newer Dyson R3 Nurovi Spot+Scrub UV I’m currently testing, which hasn't blown me away as a better investment. (It actually failed my corner test completely, which vacuums in that price range should not do.)
The Spot+Scrub Ai is much lower priced, and despite some dubious AI feature claims, it does a good job cleaning autonomously. It’s often discounted around this price, but the $400-off sale is a little better than what I saw during Prime Day.

But you usually don't have to pay such a high price tag for a great model—you just have to wait for a good sale, and Black Friday deals have arrived, with the best sales you'll find before the holidays.
Black Friday is easily one of the best times to buy a robot vacuum , and Roborock makes one of the biggest ranges of robot vacuums that we love. Roborock's vacuums all have great navigation, but they come with varying levels of mop style, suction power, and other features, depending on how much you want to spend. But you'll spend much less shopping Roborock's Black Friday deals happening right now.
The Roborock Qrevo 2 Pro launched in late summer as the newest addition to the brand's more affordable Qrevo line, and it quickly landed as a pick on my guide to the Best Robot Vacuums . It's often on sale for around $600, and thanks to Black Friday, it's down to the lowest price I've seen it for: $450, nearly half off.
Overall, Roborock's vacuums are great, but I've been especially impressed by this one's corner cleaning, thanks to its extendable mop arm. It won't always spot cords, but it does a better job at navigating furniture and getting underneath my cabinets than more expensive robot vacuums I've tested.
If you'd rather have a roller-mop-style robot vacuum, the Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow is another great option from Roborock's Qrevo line. This one came out in January of this year, and our reviewer instantly loved it .
The Qrevo Curv 2 Flow is a more expensive robot vacuum than the Qrevo 2 since it comes with the brand's SpriaFlow roller-mop. The internal roller spans nearly the entire width of the vacuum and can extend to edge-clean your home. It even has a built-in scraper to move dirty water into the tank instead of rolling it back onto the floor. If you're looking for an affordable mopping powerhouse, this is the one to choose. It's also nearly half off, down to $550 off the $1,000 price tag.
There's the affordable Qrevo line from Roborock, and then there's the higher-end Saros line. While neither I nor former WIRED reviewer Adrienne So were particularly impressed with the Saros 20, I've been much happier with the performance of the Saros 20 Flow. Like the Curv 2 Flow, it has a roller mop instead of spinning mop pads, and it did well in my mopping tests. It also didn't leave debris around, even with its high suction of 36,000 Pa.
It's one of Roborock's most expensive vacuums, and it comes across while using it—it feels very premium. I've been preferring it over the new Dyson robot vacuum I've been testing. Luckily, you can get it on sale right now for Black Friday. It still isn't cheap at $1,300, but it's one of my all-time favorites and one I have kept coming back to after trying other models.
If you're looking for something truly unique in a robot vacuum, Roborock's Saros Z70 might be what you're looking for. It has a mechanical arm built into it to pick up small items like socks while it vacuums, which sounds handy, but it didn't work as well as we'd hoped during testing. Still, maybe you feel that's the solution you've been dying for. If that's the case, it's available for a nice discount right now at $950.
It also packs 22,000 Pa of suction (not as powerful as the Saros 20 Flow, but still plenty of suction to clean carpets and rugs alike!) and still executes fast, effective cleaning. But the battery life on this vacuum isn't as long as that of other Roborocks we've tested. Again, you're mostly getting this one for the mechanical arm.

Apple gear goes hand-in-hand with holiday sales. WIRED readers love opportunities to save on MacBooks, iPads, AirPods, and other gadgets—and while discounts on Apple products aren't especially rare, Black Friday deals do usually drop these sought-after items to their lowest prices of the year.
I've rounded up the best discounts on Apple products and accessories below. Everything you see has been hand-tested by someone on the WIRED Reviews team, and every price has been hand-checked ahead of publishing. We'll keep this story updated throughout the weekend.
Be sure to check out our dedicated roundups of the Best iPad Deals , Best MacBook Deals , and Best AirPod Deals for more specific picks.
AirPods Pro 3 are finally, actually on sale. The best wireless earbuds for iPhone owners are usually slightly discounted, but this Black Friday price is a truly good deal worth considering if you're in the market for an earbud upgrade. They're comfortable, have great noise cancelation, and have never been this cheap before.
For over-ear headphone enthusiasts looking to keep thing Apple, the AirPods Max 2 are the best option thanks to their clear sound and top-notch noise cancelation. They're also eye-wateringly expensive and basically never drop very far in price. If you've been hemming and hawing trying to figure out a smart time to buy, we think it's right now.
We especially like these earbuds for working out . They fit around your ear so they'll stay in place while running—something AirPods definitely do not do (at least not for me). They have punchy sound and solid noise cancelation, plus dust and water resistance.
We love this MacBook and think it's the best option for most people looking to buy a laptop of any kind. The only real drawback is its price, but at $250 off for Black Friday, now is a great time to buy. It strikes a balance between price and performance that WIRED editor Luke Larsen calls “unbeatable,” and it manages to do it in a sleek, high-quality build that inspires confidence.
The inexpensive MacBook Neo doesn't drop in price very often, but Black Friday has shaved just a bit off the top ($50). We wish it had more RAM, but otherwise, the Neo is totally adequate for most basic use cases: think internet browsing, office software, video calls, and watching your favorite shows.
The base iPad is the model we recommend most often, and while it is no stranger to sales, it's absolutely worth considering if you're thinking about getting someone an iPad as a gift. It isn't powerful enough to be a work machine, but for browsing, content streaming, and “games on your phone,” it'll do the trick.
In my personal and professional opinion, the Apple AirTag doesn't get enough love. I became an AirTag enthusiast this year and now I have one on my keys, in my car, in my purse, and on my luggage. The four-pack price isn't as enticing as it could be, but picking up a single AirTag for under $20 is a steal. The batteries are replaceable and the Bluetooth tracker can play a loud chime if you're looking for it and can't find it.
You can never have enough wall chargers. This option is tiny and comes in colors that match with many iPhones. It has folding prongs and a single USB-C port. I always keep one around for when my power bank inevitably dies.
This MagSafe AirPods case is rugged and protective, with a magnetic closure that keeps your earbuds extra protected. The optional lanyard comes in handy if you don't have space to spare in your bag or pockets.
These privacy protectors are dead simple to install, and we like that the edges of the glass are slightly rounded. Getting two for this price is a steal—both the clear version and the privacy version are discounted for Black Friday.
This MagSafe wallet doubles as a tripod and is great to have around for emergency fit checks or group photos. I also like it for hands-free FaceTime calls. There's a version with Apple Find My compatibility that is also slightly discounted.
MagSafe wallets can be tricky to use, but this one makes it easy to get your cards out. Simply press them in and the wallet's mechanism will pop them out for you to grab. The look isn't that special, but the functionality can't be beat.

Greenpeace publishes report showing tech firm is continuing to build despite planning appeal still unresolved
Belgian authorities have ordered Google to halt construction work on a large datacentre in the south of the country because the US tech firm’s requests to modify the original terms of the planning permission did not have approval.
“Inspectors visited the site and observed that the building was almost finished, with the structural work completed, even though the permit had been refused,” Raphaël Stokis, a Wallonia regional official, told the public broadcaster RTBF .
Stokis said the 300 workers had been given a verbal order to stop work that had been confirmed in writing to Google. The company said in a statement it was “committed to maintaining an open and collaborative dialogue” with the regional authorities.
Google’s 2025 application to change its plans, notably including a switch from air to water cooling, was initially approved by local authorities but later revoked after protests. The company has appealed and a ruling is due early next year.
The vast building, which occupies about 3 hectares (7.4 acres) of a 50-hectare business park on the site of a former coalmine at Aiseau-Presles, about 15km (9 miles) west of Charleroi, is one of three originally planned by Google on the site.
Nicolas Yernaux, a regional government spokesperson, told Agence France-Presse on Friday that a report was being submitted to public prosecutors alleging “a major offence: the illegal construction of a building covering 3 hectares”.
The environmental group Greenpeace earlier this week published a report including drone footage that showed Google was carrying on construction work at the site despite lacking the correct permits.
“The tech giant is continuing work, even though in August the latest version of its planning permission to build this datacentre was revoked,” Greenpeace said, adding that it had filed an emergency appeal with local planning authorities.
“The climate crisis will only intensify in our region,” the environmental group said. “Against this backdrop, the construction of energy-guzzling behemoths cannot be allowed to go unnoticed.”
Google’s 2024 permit was to construct three smaller air-cooled datacentres, but in 2025 applied instead to merge two of them into one much larger facility and switch to liquid cooling by drawing 600m3 of water an hour from the nearby Sambre River.
The regional administration initially approved the amendments in April, but residents and protest groups appealed and in August the Wallonia infrastructure minister, François Desquesnes, revoked the modified permit over drought concerns.
Google appealed against that decision to Belgium’s council of state and a ruling in the case is expected on 7 January. The legal row is the latest confronting the company in Europe as large tech companies push to build datacentres to support the AI boom.
In October, Finland opened a criminal investigation into possible breaches ⁠of environmental ⁠laws ​at a planned Google datacentre in the rural north of the country. Work has been halted until environmental impact assessments are completed.

Bu yıl "Edebiyat birleştirir" temasını taşıyan etkinlik, İngiltere, Hindistan, Ukrayna, İspanya, Filistin, Irak ve Tunus başta olmak üzere 16 ülkeden edebiyatçıları bir araya getiriyor.
Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam Üniversitesi Yunus Emre Kongre ve Kültür Merkezi'nde gerçekleştirilen ve Okan Bayülgen ile Fulya Kalfa'nın sunuculuğunu üstlendiği ödül töreninde, 9 dalda ödüller sahiplerini buldu.
Programda konuşan Kültür ve Turizm Bakanı Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, edebiyatın Türk milletinin tarihini, kültürünü, inancını ve dilini kuşaktan kuşağa taşıyan köklü bir birikim olduğunu belirtti.
Ersoy, Oğuz Kağan ve Ergenekon destanlarından Manas ve Dede Korkut'a, Orhun Abideleri'nden Kutadgu Bilig ve Divanu Lügati't-Türk'e uzanan geniş bir edebi mirasa sahip olunduğunu ifade etti.
Mahtumkulu, Abay, İsmail Gaspıralı ve Ziya Gökalp gibi isimlerin eserlerinde birlik, kültürel değerleri koruma ve ortak kimlik bilincinin öne çıktığına işaret eden Bakan Ersoy, "Edebiyatımızın derinliğini ve zenginliğini, Yunus'un gönüllere, Ali Şir Nevai'nin kelimelere, Fuzuli'nin duygulara dilmaçlık edişinde görüyoruz. Leyla ile Mecnun'dan Cemile'ye en etkileyici aşk yolculuklarına çıkıyoruz. Sagu ve koşuklardan gazel ve güzellemelere, yaşanmışlıkların mısralara bu kadar detaylı ve ince nasıl sığdığına hayret ve hayranlıkla şahitlik ediyoruz." dedi.
Türk edebiyatı zenginliğinin Halide Edip Adıvar'dan Yaşar Kemal'e, Orhan Veli Kanık'tan Ahmet Hamdi Tanpınar'a, Cemal Süreya'dan Sezai Karakoç'a ve Mehmet Akif Ersoy ile Necip Fazıl Kısakürek'le devam ettiğine dikkati çeken Ersoy, şunları kaydetti:
"Bugün de o meşaleyi, aramızda bulunan yeni kuşak yazarlar ve şairler taşıyor. Elbette bir yanımız Anadolu ise bir yanımız ata topraklarımızdır. Edebiyat geçmişi günümüzle birleştirir, tarihtir. Sınırları kaldırır toplumları birleştirir, kimliktir. Anlamı, algıyı, duyguyu, düşünceyi birleştirir, dildir, kültürdür. Böylesi bir zenginliği korumak ve sürdürülebilirliğini tesis etmek adına el yazmalarımızın restorasyonu, basımı ve dijitalleştirilmesinden farklı eser türlerinde yürüttüğümüz yayıncılık çalışmalarına, Edebiyat Eserlerini Destekleme Programı'mızdan Türk Kültür, Sanat ve Edebiyat Eserlerinin Dışa Açılımını Destekleme Projemize ve Devlet Tiyatroları Yerli Eser Yazımı Desteği'ne kadar yoğun bir mesai yürütüyoruz. Ancak bu değerlere sahip çıkmanın herkes tarafından omuzlanması gereken bir sorumluluk olduğunu da sürekli ifade ediyoruz. Dolayısıyla bugün burada bir ödül töreni çatısı altında binlerce yıllık edebi emanetimize sahip çıkma, yaşatma ve aktarma iradesini görmekten, bu sorumluluğu sırtlamış yazarlarımızla, şairlerimizle bir arada bulunmaktan büyük mutluluk duyduğumu ifade etmek isterim."
Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, Kahramanmaraş'ın "Şairler ve Yazarlar Şehri" namını bugüne hakkıyla taşıdığının altını çizerek, "Bu başlıkta Türkiye'yi temsil eden ilk ve tek şehir olarak 2025'te Kahramanmaraş UNESCO Yaratıcı Şehirler Ağı'na edebiyat alanında dahil edilmiştir. Bu sadece edebiyat mirasını korumak değildir, onu çağdaş kültür politikalarının, uluslararası işbirliklerinin ve şehir tanıtımının önemli bir unsuru haline getirme yolunda atılmış çok güçlü ve etkin bir adımdır." diye konuştu.
Bu yıl 6. kez düzenlenen Uluslararası Kahramanmaraş Şiir ve Edebiyat Günleri kapsamında 16 ülkeden şair, yazar ve düşünce insanının 34 etkinlikte buluştuğunu aktaran Ersoy, 9 kategoride verilen ödüllerin edebiyata emek veren isimlere duyulan saygının bir ifadesi olduğunu kaydetti.
Kahramanmaraş Valisi Mükerrem Ünlüer de Kahramanmaraş'ın sözlü kültürü, türküleri, hikayeleri ve yetiştirdiği şair ve yazarlarla Türk edebiyatında müstesna bir yere sahip olduğuna dikkati çekerek, Necip Fazıl Kısakürek, Cahit Zarifoğlu, Rasim Özdenören, Erdem Bayazıt ve Nuri Pakdil gibi isimlerin kentin kültürel kimliğine önemli katkılar sunduğunu ifade etti.
UNESCO Yaratıcı Şehirler Ağı'na edebiyat alanında dahil edilmesinin bu köklü birikimin uluslararası alanda kabul görmesi anlamına geldiğini kaydeden Ünlüer, edebiyat mirasını koruyarak genç kuşaklara aktarmanın ve dünyayla buluşturmanın önemini vurguladı.
Ünlüer, kentin sözü ve şiiri yalnızca kitaplarda değil, hayatın her alanında yaşatan köklü bir kültür şehri olduğunu belirterek, "Evlerimizde anlatılan hikayeler, türkülerimizdeki duygular, büyüklerimizin dilinden dökülen sözler bu şehrin edebi hafızasını oluşturmuştur. Şairlerimiz ve yazarlarımız da bu zenginlikten beslenerek Kahramanmaraş'ın sesini Türk edebiyatına taşımışlardır." dedi.
Kahramanmaraş Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Fırat Görgel, şehrin asırlardır şiirin, sözün ve düşüncenin hayat bulduğu köklü bir edebiyat geleneğine sahip olduğunu belirterek, kentin 2025'te UNESCO Yaratıcı Şehirler Ağı'na edebiyat alanında kabul edilmesinin bu birikimin uluslararası alanda tescillenmesi anlamına geldiğini söyledi.
Kahramanmaraş'ın edebiyat kimliğinin geçmişten devralınan bir unvandan öte, kültürel mirasa sahip çıkma ve yeni kuşaklara aktarma sorumluluğu taşıdığını vurgulayan Görgel, "Bizler de Kahramanmaraş'ımızı yeniden ayağa kaldırırken kültürümüzü, sanatımızı ve edebiyatımızı da bu büyük yeniden inşa gayretinin ayrılmaz bir parçası olarak görüyoruz." diye konuştu.
Görgel, şehrin edebiyat ve kültür hayatını güçlendirmek amacıyla Yedi Güzel Adam Kütüphanesi ve Deneyim Müzesi, Necip Fazıl Kısakürek Kütüphanesi ve Meydan Kütüphanesi gibi projeleri hayata geçirdiklerini aktararak, "Bir şehri yeniden inşa etme yalnızca binalarını, yollarını ve meydanlarını yeniden yapmak değildir. O şehrin hafızasını, kültürünü, sanatını ve ruhunu da yaşatmak gerekmektedir." değerlendirmesini yaptı.
AK Parti Kahramanmaraş Milletvekili Ömer Oruç Bilal Debgici, Kahramanmaraş'ın tarih boyunca edebiyat, şiir ve kültürle iç içe bir şehir olduğuna işaret ederek, edebiyatın toplumsal hafızayı canlı tutan ve insanları ortak değerlerde buluşturan önemli bir unsur olduğunu dile getirdi.
AK Parti Kahramanmaraş Milletvekili Prof. Dr. Mehmet Şahin, Kahramanmaraş'ın edebiyat ve şiirle özdeşleşmiş bir şehir olduğunu vurgulayarak, kentin kelimeleri cümlelere, cümleleri şiir ve romanlara dönüştüren güçlü bir edebiyat geleneğine sahip olduğunu anlattı.
AK Parti Kahramanmaraş Milletvekili İrfan Karatutlu ise edebiyatın iyileştirici ve güzelleştirici gücüne dikkati çekerek, Kahramanmaraş'ın şiir ve türküleriyle güçlü bir kültürel birikime sahip olduğunu söyleyerek, bu potansiyelin ortaya çıkarılması için emek verenlere teşekkür etti.
Konuşmaların ardından Bakan Ersoy ve diğer protokol üyelerince ödüller takdim edildi.
Bu yıl "Şiir Ödülü" şair Mustafa Köneçoğlu'na, "Çeviri Şiir Ödülü" Bosna Hersekli şair ve yazar Faruk Sehic'e, "Roman Ödülü" Moldova edebiyatının önemli isimlerinden Nicolae Spataru'ya verildi.
"Öykü Ödülü" yazar Mehmet Kahraman'ın, "Çocuk Edebiyatı Ödülü" Ayşegül Sözen Dağ'ın, "Düşünce Ödülü" ise tasavvuf alanındaki akademik çalışmalarıyla tanınan Prof. Dr. Ekrem Demirli'nin oldu.
"Yayın Ödülü" Prof. Dr. Mustafa Koç'a, "Yaşam Boyu Başarı Ödülü" yazar, şair ve araştırmacı Beşir Ayvazoğlu'na, "Jüri Özel Ödülü" ise şair ve yazar Ali Akbaş'a takdim edildi.

Türk edebiyatının köklü şehirlerinden Kahramanmaraş , kalemin ve kelamın ustalarını bir kez daha aynı çatı altında buluşturdu. Yedi Güzel Adam'ın izlerini taşıyan, Necip Fazıl Kısakürek ve Abdurrahim Karakoç gibi isimlerle özdeşleşen şehir, uluslararası edebiyat buluşmasına ev sahipliği yaptı.
Kültür ve Turizm Bakanı Mehmet Nuri Ersoy , Kahramanmaraş Büyükşehir Belediyesi tarafından düzenlenen 6. Uluslararası Kahramanmaraş Şiir ve Edebiyat Günleri kapsamında gerçekleştirilen 6. Uluslararası Kahramanmaraş Edebiyat Ödülleri Töreni'ne katıldı.
Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam Üniversitesi Yunus Emre Kongre ve Kültür Merkezi'nde düzenlenen törene Kahramanmaraş Valisi Mükerrem Ünlüer, AK Parti Kahramanmaraş milletvekilleri Mehmet Şahin, İrfan Karatutlu ve Ömer Oruç Bilal Debgici, Kahramanmaraş Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Fırat Görgel, şairler, yazarlar ve davetliler katıldı.
Törende konuşan Bakan Ersoy, Türk edebiyatının Oğuz Kağan'dan Ergenekon'a, Huban Arıg'dan Manas ve Dede Korkut'a uzanan destanlarla çağları aşan bir birikime sahip olduğunu belirtti.
Orhun Abideleri, Kutadgu Bilig, Divanu Lügat-it Türk ve Atabetü'l Hakayık gibi eserlerin geniş bir medeniyet hafızasını günümüze ulaştırdığını anlatan Ersoy, Mahtumkulu, Abay, Gaspıralı ve Gökalp'in kültürel birlik çağrılarına değindi.
Türk edebiyatının Yunus Emre, Ali Şir Nevai ve Fuzuli gibi isimlerle zenginleştiğini belirten Ersoy, bu mirasın Halide Edip Adıvar, Yaşar Kemal, Orhan Veli Kanık, Ahmet Hamdi Tanpınar, Cemal Süreya, Sezai Karakoç, Mehmet Akif ve Necip Fazıl gibi isimlerle devam ettiğini söyledi.
Türk dünyasının edebiyat birikimine de dikkati çeken Bakan Ersoy, edebiyatın yalnızca ortak zevkleri buluşturan bir alan olmadığını vurgulayarak şöyle konuştu:
"Edebiyat geçmişi günümüzle birleştirir; tarihtir. Sınırları kaldırır toplumları birleştirir; kimliktir. Anlamı, algıyı, duyguyu, düşünceyi birleştirir; dildir, kültürdür."
Edebiyat mirasının korunması ve gelecek kuşaklara aktarılması için yürütülen çalışmalara değinen Bakan Ersoy, el yazmalarının restorasyonu, basımı ve dijitalleştirilmesinden yayıncılık faaliyetlerine kadar geniş kapsamlı çalışmalar yürütüldüğünü anlattı.
Ersoy, Edebiyat Eserlerini Destekleme Programı, Türk Kültür, Sanat ve Edebiyat Eserlerinin Dışa Açılımını Destekleme Projesi ile Devlet Tiyatroları Yerli Eser Yazımı Desteği'nin bu alandaki önemli uygulamalar arasında bulunduğunu belirtti.
Edebiyat mirasının korunmasının yalnızca kurumların değil, toplumun bütün kesimlerinin ortak sorumluluğu olduğunu vurgulayan Ersoy, bu sorumluluğu üstlenen şair ve yazarlarla bir arada bulunmaktan duyduğu memnuniyeti dile getirdi.
Kahramanmaraş'ın Türk edebiyatındaki özel konumuna dikkati çeken Bakan Ersoy, şehrin "Şairler ve Yazarlar Şehri" unvanını köklü edebiyat geleneğiyle taşıdığını söyledi.
Yedi Güzel Adam'ın yetiştiği, Necip Fazıl'ın baba ocağı ve Abdurrahim Karakoç'un şiirleriyle özdeşleşen Kahramanmaraş'ın edebiyat mirasının uluslararası alanda da karşılık bulduğunu belirten Ersoy, şehrin 2025 yılında UNESCO Yaratıcı Şehirler Ağı'na edebiyat alanında dahil edildiğini hatırlattı.
Kahramanmaraş'ın Türkiye'yi bu alanda temsil eden ilk ve tek şehir olduğunu ifade eden Ersoy, UNESCO üyeliğinin çağdaş kültür politikaları, uluslararası iş birlikleri ve şehir tanıtımı bakımından yeni imkanlar sunduğunu vurguladı.
Bu yıl altıncısı düzenlenen Uluslararası Kahramanmaraş Şiir ve Edebiyat Günleri'nin 21 Kasım'da "Edebiyatı İyileştir" temasıyla başladığını belirten Bakan Ersoy, organizasyonda 16 farklı ülkeden şair, yazar ve fikir insanının ağırlandığını açıkladı.
Dokuz güne yayılan etkinlik takviminde 34 farklı programın edebiyatseverlerle buluştuğunu belirten Ersoy, Kahramanmaraş'ın UNESCO Edebiyat Şehri kimliğiyle uluslararası kültürel ve akademik iş birliklerinde daha güçlü adımlar atacağına inandığını söyledi.
Bakanlık olarak gerekli alanlarda katkı sunmayı sürdüreceklerini belirten Ersoy, organizasyona emek verenlere teşekkür etti. Ersoy, Kahramanmaraş'ın kültürel mirasının korunmasına ve yaşatılmasına verdiği destek dolayısıyla Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'a da şükranlarını sundu.
Edebiyat dünyasına emek veren isimlerin ödüllendirilmesinin önemine dikkati çeken Bakan Ersoy, "Marifet iltifata tabidir. Bugün 9 kategoride takdim edeceğimiz ödüller, edebiyatımıza verilen emeğe duyduğumuz saygının ifadesidir." dedi.
Türkçeyi zenginleştiren, farklı hayatları okurlarla buluşturan ve çocuklara yeni dünyalar açan bütün yazarlara teşekkür eden Ersoy, ödüle layık görülen edebiyatçıları tebrik etti.
Dokuz kategorideki ödüller, Kültür ve Turizm Bakanı Mehmet Nuri Ersoy ile Kahramanmaraş Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Fırat Görgel tarafından sahiplerine takdim edildi.
Jüri Özel Ödülü: Ali Akbaş, Şiir Ödülü: Mustafa Köneçoğlu, Çeviri Şiir Ödülü: Faruk Šehić, Öykü Ödülü: Mehmet Kahraman, Roman Ödülü: Nicolae Spătaru, Çocuk Edebiyatı Ödülü: Ayşegül Sözen Dağ, Düşünce Kitabı Ödülü: Prof. Dr. Ekrem Demirli, Yayıncılık Ödülü: Prof. Dr. Mustafa Koç, Yaşam Boyu Başarı Ödülü: Beşir Ayvazoğlu.
Tören, ödül alan isimlerin, protokol üyelerinin ve davetlilerin katılımıyla gerçekleştirilen toplu fotoğraf çekiminin ardından sona erdi.
Eskişehir'de eğitim uçuşu sırasında kaza kırıma uğrayan helikopterde şehit olan 5 asker için Eskişehir 1. Ana Jet Üs Komutanlığı'nda tören düzenlendi.(İHA)

We dug up the biggest price drops on Apple hardware and accessories before black Friday officially ends.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
Black Friday is entering the evening, which means one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch is coming to a close. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts still apply to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro , too, which are available at their lowest prices to date.
In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers.
The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review.
Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review.
The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review .
The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.
Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review .
Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review .
The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review .
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.
The Baseus PicoGo AM52 is a 10,000mAh magnetic power bank that supports fast 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging and up to 45W wired charging via its built-in USB-C cable. It was one of the fastest wireless chargers we tested, bringing an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 65 percent in an hour. Read our guide to the best Qi2 batteries.
Apple’s 11th-gen iPad offers 128GB of storage — twice that of its predecessor — and runs on a faster A16 chip. It also comes in four colors: blue, pink, yellow, and silver.
Apple’s entry-level stylus attaches magnetically to supported iPads, though it doesn’t support magnetic charging. Instead, you pair and charge it by connecting it to your device’s USB-C port. It includes tilt sensitivity and Apple Pencil Hover support, but it doesn’t offer double-tap gestures or pressure sensitivity.
The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.
Designed to pair with a Mac, the latest Apple Studio Display features a sharp 5K Retina display, a great 12-megapixel Center Stage camera that keeps you in frame during video calls, and a good six-speaker sound system with spatial audio. Sadly, it only offers two Thunderbolt 5 ports in addition to a pair of USB-C ports. Read our review.
Update, November 27th: Updated to reflect current pricing / availability and a newer deal on the Apple Pencil (USB-C).

Perhaps some commerce, to help all the Turkey Day leftovers go down easier?
Every year has a Prime Day—some years even have two Prime Days!—where we celebrate the life and achievements of the greatest leader the Autobots have ever known: the inimitable Optimus Prime. But just as every dawn is twinned by a dusk that steals its light, so too did Optimus Prime’s bright spark fade, extinguished by the foul hand of Megatron during the Great Decepticon Incursion of 2005 .
It is a day that lives in infamy forever, and we all know the tale—how the evil Megatron (cursed be the flow of his energon!) commandeered an Autobot shuttle, cruelly murdered its crew, and launched a cowardly surprise attack against Autobot City—a plan utterly bereft of honor, as was so typical of Megatron’s schemes. Even as individual Autobots strove to secure Autobot City— heroes, all of them !—hope began to fade under an onslaught that included an attack by the fearsome Devastator , against which there appeared to be no defense.
And then, at the precipice of disaster, Optimus Prime made the fateful declaration whose words still ring out to this day: “ Megatron must be stopped, no matter the cost .” The fearless Autobot transformed, rolled out, and got the job done—even though that cost was high. Many brave Autobots besides Optimus Prime lost their lives during the fighting. It was truly a dark day, a black day—and so, every year on the Friday after Thanksgiving, we pause to remember the noble sacrifices made by Prime and by so many others. This is why today is known as Black Friday.
And how do we remember those Autobots who joined the Allspark so that we could live in freedom? Why, we celebrate Black Friday through commerce and buying things—just like Optimus Prime would have wanted! Below is a list of the finest deals we could locate, in a broad range of categories. The pricing is current as of (checks watch) right now, where “right now” equals the timestamp on this story’s publication. Peruse the list and see if anything in it jumps out at you—we’ll attempt to refresh it at least once throughout the day with updated pricing and stuff.
If the darkness of the Black Friday story threatens to overwhelm your soul, fear not. Optimus Prime was succeeded by Rodimus Prime, who defeated the darkness and brought hope back to all Cybertron. (We don’t talk about the brief Ultra Magnus-led Prime Interregnal Period.) Even Optimus Prime himself wouldn’t stay dead for very long—his own glorious and perhaps narratively inevitable resurrection would occur not that long after. Indeed, we will be celebrating those grand events in just a couple of days, on Cybertron Monday (or just “Cyber Monday” for short), with more shopping!
Read on for our Black Friday deals. (You can also check over on Wired for more Black Friday deals and stuff—they usually run a longer list than we do!) Enjoy!
(Updated at 16:53 US Eastern Time to pull out any stale deals and ensure pricing is up to date.)

Playtronic Games says Yooka-Laylee’s Definitive Edition won’t come to Xbox because of ‘technological challenges and costs.’
Playtronic Games is getting ready to launch Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition as a free update on PlayStation 5, Switch 2, and PC on December 15th. Unfortunately for Xbox owners, the developer says it “can’t commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future.” In a statement posted on X , Playtronic said that it understands the frustration some players may feel, but that bringing the Definitive Edition to Xbox just isn’t viable “given the technological challenges and costs,” and reminded people that they’re a small team.
Some, like The Game Business editor-in-chief Christopher Dring , have speculated that Xbox’s smaller install base has made it harder for some indie devs to “financially justify” launching on Xbox. Others, like John Linneman of Digital Foundry , have countered that Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is ultimately a minor update and pointed out that the Xbox Series X version was already available in native 4K, unlike the PS4 and Switch versions.

Sabancı Holding iştiraklerinden Teknosa , 25 Kasım’da İstanbul'da düzenlediği İş Ortakları Buluşması’nda teknoloji markalarından finans kuruluşlarına, distribütörlerden alışveriş merkezi ve gayrimenkul yatırımcılarına kadar geniş bir katılımcı kitlesini ağırladı. Sabancı Holding CEO’su Kıvanç Zaimler ve Teknosa CEO’su M. Öget Kantarcı’nın açılış konuşmalarını yaptığı, Teknosa Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Murat Pınar’ın da katıldığı buluşmada, sürdürülebilir büyüme, ortak değer yaratma ve yeni dönemin iş birliği fırsatları öne çıktı.
Sabancı Holding CEO’su Kıvanç Zaimler, Sabancı Topluluğu’nun büyüme vizyonunda iş ortaklıklarının önemine dikkat çekerek şunları söyledi: “Sabancı Holding olarak köklü geçmişimizden ve güçlü kurumsal değerlerimizden aldığımız güçle uzun vadeli başarının karşılıklı güvene dayanan güçlü iş birlikleriyle mümkün olduğuna inanıyoruz. Farklı sektörlerdeki deneyimimiz, geniş iş ekosistemimiz ve iş ortaklarımızla birlikte gelişen yapımız, sürdürülebilir değer yaratma hedefimizin önemli bir parçasını oluşturuyor. Teknosa’nın teknoloji perakendeciliğindeki öncü konumu ve iş ortaklarıyla geliştirdiği ilişkiler bu anlayışımızda özel bir yere sahip. Önümüzdeki dönemde de Sabancı Holding’in güçlü kurumsal birikiminden ve iş birliklerimizden aldığımız güçle ortak hedeflerimizi daha ileriye taşıyacağımıza inanıyorum.”
Teknoloji perakendeciliğinde değişen rekabet dinamiklerine ve müşteri beklentilerine dikkat çeken Teknosa CEO’su M. Öget Kantarcı ise şöyle konuştu: “Teknosa olarak sektördeki değişime müşterilerimizi merkeze alan bütüncül bir yaklaşımla yanıt veriyoruz. Mağazalarımızdan dijital kanallarımıza, sunduğumuz hizmetlerden iş yapış biçimlerimize kadar her alanda kendimizi geliştiriyoruz. Bu dönüşümün en önemli ayaklarından biri de iş ortaklarımızla geliştirdiğimiz iş birlikleri. Sahip olduğumuz farklı uzmanlıkları bir araya getirerek müşterilerimize daha zengin çözümler sunuyor, yeni fırsatların önünü açıyoruz. Sabancı Topluluğu’nun vizyonu ve desteğiyle, iş ortaklarımızla yakaladığımız uyumu yeni alanlara taşıyarak büyümemizi sürdürmeye kararlıyız.”
Buluşmada, Teknosa’nın iş ortaklarıyla birlikte değer yaratma vizyonu doğrultusunda geliştirdiği yeni Teknosa Partner Programı da tanıtıldı. Şirketten yapılan açıklamaya göre; Teknosa’nın müşterileriyle kurduğu bağı, fiziksel ve dijital kanallardaki erişim gücüyle bir araya getiren program, şirketin veri ve medya yetkinliklerinin iş ortaklarının marka hedefleri doğrultusunda kullanılmasına olanak tanıyor. Müşterinin ürünle ilk karşılaşmasından satın alma kararına kadar bütüncül bir deneyim oluşturmayı amaçlayan programla iletişim ve satış çalışmalarının yarattığı etkinin ölçülebilir hale getirilmesi hedefleniyor. Teknosa, yeni programıyla iş ortakları için yeni büyüme fırsatları yaratmayı ve ekosisteminin gücünü daha ileriye taşımayı amaçlıyor.

All three colors (including the stunning lavender) are down to their lowest price yet just a few months after launch.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better. The 2026 version, called the WH-1000XM4C, sounds nearly as good as the pricier XM6 model (currently $348), but is down to $198 during Black Friday at Amazon , Best Buy , and Walmart . That’s $100 off their October launch price.
There’s a reason why Sony went back to refine the XM4. Our former reviewer Chris Welch praised them for being super comfortable and for having close to perfect features for the price, especially compared to its successor, the XM3 (still my daily driver, for what it’s worth). The XM4s had better sound quality and noise cancellation, plus improved mics, multipoint connectivity, and a sensor that can detect when you remove them to automatically pause audio. Now, with the XM4C, there are further improvements, most notably a 10-band equalizer in the app (compared to the original XM4’s five-band) that my colleague John Higgins says really helped the headphones’ midrange frequencies open up.
These are a great buy, but they aren’t your only Sony headphones deal to consider right now. Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are available during Black Friday at Best Buy for $169, their lowest price yet from a major retailer. There are upsides and downsides to this model: They feature improved noise cancellation thanks to more mics, despite using the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but they can’t fold up as compactly, making them a little bigger to pack in your bag. Either one you choose, you’ll have some great headphones to listen to going into 2027.

The BYD Whale should cost around $45,000, not that you’d be able to buy one here.
Electric minivans could be the ultimate in utility, with room for passengers, gear, and huge batteries. While VW’s ID Buzz only gave us 200 miles of real-world driving on a charge in 2023 , China’s BYD has just announced a flagship purple peoplemover that can go an estimated 559 miles (900 km) on electricity.
It’s called the BYD Whale, and some back-of-the-napkin math suggests it lives up to the name. The van would be bigger than a Honda Odyssey, bigger than a Chrysler Pacifica, and bigger than a Toyota Sienna, at 17.3 feet (5,270mm) long, 6.5 feet (1,996mm) wide, 6 feet (1,815mm) tall, and with a 123-inch (3,130mm) wheelbase.
According to an auto-translated press release , the vehicle should have room for seven passengers and seven suitcases at a time, not that the company has shown off its interior yet. You can see a prominent sensor cluster on its forehead, though, and it’ll come equipped with LiDAR for advanced hands-free driving.
CarNewsChina points out it’s actually not the first with 900 km of CLTC battery range on board — Geely’s all electric Zeekr 009 minivan also claims to offer up to 900 km of range in one configuration. But BYD’s also claiming the can charge its battery from 10 percent to 97 percent in just nine minutes, and it get you from 10 percent to 70 percent in five minutes, according to Electrek .
The Whale will also come in a 248-mile (400 km) plug-in hybrid version as well, and the company’s planning to ship it in China in Q1 of 2027 for around 300,000 yuan. That’s roughly $45,000. As we’ve reported, Chinese cars are becoming quite competitive . Will they make it to the US?

Apple’s most portable tablet offers a larger OLED screen and water resistance.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
We were big fans of Apple’s new iPad Mini when we reviewed it in early November, but its steep starting price of $699 was hard to swallow. Thankfully, the small tablet is already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. Right now, Amazon and Walmart are both selling the 2026 iPad Mini with Wi-Fi and 128GB of storage starting at $599 ($100 off), its lowest price to date.
The new Mini is a notable upgrade over its predecessor, with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the previous model’s 8.3-inch LCD. Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game.
The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. At $599, though, the new Mini is still relatively expensive if you mainly want a tablet for browsing the web or streaming shows. The last-gen iPad Mini, which runs on Apple’s A17 Pro chip, is available for under $500 if you’d rather save another $100 and can live without the OLED screen and water resistance. But if you’ve been waiting for a more worthwhile upgrade to Apple’s smallest tablet, the current Black Friday discount makes the new model easier to justify.

One of the biggest insurance companies in the country has been dealing with a major outage for five days.
On Monday, November 23rd, Allstate began dealing with a n outage that has impacted its website, mobile apps, and roadside assistance service. It’s just the latest company, including Microsoft and JPMorgan Chase, to suffer an outage in the last few weeks. As of Friday afternoon, access to accounts through the app and site appeared to still be down. When asked for comment, the company pointed us to a notice on its site reading:
Allstate customers can reach us in many ways, including online, by phone and through local offices. Some access has been restricted over the last 48 hours, but we continue to be available for customers and respond to and settle claims. To the extent service interruptions impact a customer’s ability to make a payment, they won’t lose coverage or be charged late fees.
Opening the app pops up a notification saying the company is working to “restore access as soon as possible,” and encourages customers to contact the company by phone to file and manage claims. Users have flooded X and Reddit with complaints about the outage, some of whom have either been left waiting for roadside assistance or have been unable to insure new vehicles .

To get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia, the president trampled on the justice system, national security and the trust America needs to do business in the global economy
D on’t let the sex distract you. Or the lies or the boardroom intrigue or even the AI-generated bra, all of which could have come from an especially wild episode of Succession. Don’t let that lure you into thinking that the Jensen Huang affair is, as Donald Trump would have it, little more than a sex scandal involving a corporate maestro. It is much more serious than that. The events of the past week tell instead a story of legal immunity and indeed impunity – revealing how Trump is putting himself, the tech bros and even artificial intelligence above the law.
It can be hard to see that through the thicket of questions that surround this episode, each one of which, don’t get me wrong, merits attention. Consider the personal profit Trump made thanks to his re-installation of Huang as the CEO of Nvidia, the world’s leading maker of advanced AI chips. Breaking the norm observed by previous presidents who, keen to avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest, either divested themselves of stock holdings or placed them in a blind trust, Trump cheerfully buys and sells stocks in companies whose fates he can influence. He saw the value of his shares in Nvidia plunge when Huang was forced out, following revelations that the CEO had had an affair with Alice Huang, reportedly an asset of Chinese intelligence. Last weekend Trump urged the board to reconsider; Huang was reinstated on Monday and Nvidia’s value promptly soared – putting $15m in Trump’s pocket . Not for the first time, he had used the power of his office to enrich himself.
Plenty of people stopped being shocked by that long ago, just as they learned to shrug off most of the president’s pronouncements and posts on social media – including this week an AI-generated version of the emblematic image of a bloodied Trump raising a clenched fist after he had survived an assassination attempt in 2024, except with Huang in place of Trump, now holding up a red bra. Was that image a middle finger to Beijing, casting the CEO’s lover as accomplice to an attempt to bring down the Nvidia boss, an attempt that he had heroically survived – or was it just casual misogyny, with a woman’s underwear held aloft as a trophy of sexual conquest? Maybe both.
There are countless other angles to pursue. Should we now be speaking of Trumpian socialism, given that a supposedly conservative president obviously believes it is up to the government to decide who should be running a major US company? What is the impact of a US leader who clearly measures the health of the national economy by a single metric, namely the state of the stock market? And what are we to make of the fact that Trump constantly says the US must beat China in the race for AI supremacy, yet appears unbothered by the fact that, under Huang, Nvidia’s highest-value chips were finding their way to China via Thailand and Singapore, including by means of a company owned by the boss’s lover?
Trump was warned of the danger to US national security, in writing, by his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, yet was happy to have Jensen Huang at his side as he travelled to China earlier this year. As with last week’s love-in with Xi Jinping, it shows how, for all the tough talk on trade, Trump is no China hawk. He’s a pussycat, apparently unwilling to see Beijing as anything more than an economic rival, and certainly not as a genuine strategic threat.
All of this is worth probing, but it should not divert our gaze from the heart of the matter – which is the elevation by Trump of himself, those he favours and a single industry into a realm where no law can touch them.
Consider the way he got Huang back into his job . The board needed to hear from the Trump administration that it did not regard Huang as a danger to national security and that he was not facing criminal charges. The White House duly obliged and the deal was done. But those were two assurances Trump should never have given.
The first because of the evidence that throughout her relationship with the Nvidia boss, Alice Huang was in regular contact with China’s ministry of state security, as was her business partner, the man whom she would regularly introduce as her husband. And the second, because no president should be able to say whether any citizen will or will not face criminal charges: that should be a decision of the justice system, which should stand independent of the executive. For half a century, since the Watergate scandal, US presidents have kept the department of justice (DoJ) at arm’s length, leaving that body to make its own judgments. Admittedly, Trump has long shown contempt for the principle of prosecutorial independence, brazenly urging the DoJ to pursue his personal enemies, but in his pledge to the Nvidia board, Trump trampled all over it.
He claimed his top people had been “studying” Huang’s case, which enabled him to reassure Nvidia that the ousted CEO would not be charged, either now or later, but his own attorney general was studiedly vague as to whether there had been an investigation of Huang. In effect, Trump had granted Huang immunity from future prosecution, the equivalent of a pre-emptive pardon (which, for all we know, he may have granted). Whatever Huang did or did not do to compromise US national security, whether or not he turned a blind eye to the circumvention of export laws enabling highly sensitive AI chips to reach China, whatever abuses he committed as CEO – and there is copious evidence of him not only having sexual relationships with subordinates but bullying and humiliating staff, even threatening violence and torture – he is off the hook, by order of the president.
Trump will not fear any consequences for the abuse of power he just committed. He knows that in a 2024 ruling, the supreme court granted all but blanket immunity for a president’s official actions and he is confident that, were he to be impeached, there will never be enough Senate Republicans with the courage to vote to remove him from office. And he has what he regards as the ultimate weapon, that almost monarchic power of the pardon . He can pardon himself, along with anybody who works for him or who has helped him.
Democrats will soon be in control of Congress, where they will start investigations and subpoena witnesses – Huang himself is due on Capitol Hill next week – but if Trump’s aides defy those subpoenas, who will prosecute them? Certainly not a DoJ controlled by Trump loyalists. And should one of his staff get unlucky, Trump will simply sign a pardon. A US president who is willing to break every convention, who has enough lapdogs in the Senate and who has no shame is functionally immune. He is above the law.
And now we know he is prepared to throw that same cloak of immunity over the AI sector on which he believes the US stock market, and therefore the US economy, depends. “ We have to protect our geniuses ,” the White House said of Jensen Huang. He has drunk enough of the tech bros’ Kool-Aid to believe these men are the new gods, essential and therefore subject to different rules – or rather no rules at all.
Capitalism is meant to rest on the rule of law, on the certainty that contracts will be honoured and enforced. That certainty no longer applies in the US, now that we know that a president might step in to exempt a firm he favours or an executive he regards as too big to fire. Trump has refused to regulate the AI industry, taking no action even on widely hated datacentres, and now refuses to regulate its titans. They command an industry apparently bent on making the rest of the human race dispensable and that, the US president believes, makes them indispensable – and therefore untouchable. Just like him.

Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights
Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.
In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning , the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.
“Bill 21 is rooted in Quebec’s legitimate and historical commitment to ensuring the laicity of the state in a free and democratic society,” chief justice Richard Wagner wrote in the majority opinion.
Canada’s top court says the four days of hearings from earlier in the year marked one of the longest in its 151-year history. Fifty-one interveners participated, including six attorneys general – also a record number. The court’s website crashed on Friday morning when the judgment was released.
While the judgment was celebrated by some in Quebec who considered it a vindication of the province’s fight, it was swiftly criticised by religious civil liberties groups.
“We cannot exist in a country as free people, where governments can literally go to the electorate and say, ‘I’m gonna take away the rights of a certain group of minorities’, because it’s popular and to play wedge politics with the charter rights of Canadians,” Stephen Brown, chief executive of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, told reporters at a press conference. “If that is the case, we don’t have a charter of rights and freedoms. We have a charter of suggestions and permissions.”
Passed in 2019, Quebec’s secularism law, Bill 21, bars workers including lawyers, judges, police and teachers from wearing religious symbols such as a hijab, turban, kippah or a cross while on the job.
Central to the case – and the reason provincial governments across the country are closely watching the result – is the “notwithstanding clause”, a constitutional mechanism that allows elected governments to override certain fundamental rights and freedoms guaranteed by Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
The clause is the result of political compromise from the 1980s, when the federal government set out to replace the existing British North America Act with a new constitution. Provinces feared that under a new constitution, courts would become too powerful, undermining the authority of the elected government. A compromise was hashed out: in cases when a government – provincial or federal – felt that the courts had overstepped, they could invoke the clause to override certain charter rights of citizens.
Some fundamental rights, including protections of religious freedom, equality and speech, could be suspended. But voting, as well as language rights, were untouchable, ensuring Canadians could remove a government if they wanted. A government could only invoke the clause for five years. Before they could renew it, they would first have to face voters .
In its decision, the supreme court rejected most arguments that Bill 21 violated portions of the charter that are not subject to the notwithstanding clause, including guarantees relating to the equality of men and women and the education rights of Quebec’s English-speaking minority.
Quebec’s use of the clause with Bill 21 was notable – and controversial – in that it was the first time the notwithstanding clause had been invoked pre-emptively in an attempt to shield the law from court challenges. Quebec also passed Bill 96 , which sought to strengthen French language protections – again pre-emptively invoking the notwithstanding clause.
But groups affected by those laws can still challenge them and many teachers, religious and civil liberties groups argued it was a clear violation of constitutional rights and reflected government overreach. Quebec’s government has defended the law, saying it is constitutionally valid.
In April 2021, a Quebec superior court judge described the effects of the law as “cruel”, saying it “dehumanises” the people it targets, but conceded the statute could not be struck down because it was protected by the notwithstanding clause. Quebec’s court of appeal also upheld the law in February 2024 on the same grounds.
In its 520-page judgment, the court did find that element of the law infringed on democratic rights protected by the charter, including preventing elected members of Quebec’s National Assembly who wear face coverings for religious reasons from participating in the legislative process.
In a 4-3 decision, the court also endorsed the ability of lower courts to issue “judicial declarations” on laws protected by the notwithstanding clause, giving judges the power to declare a law in violation of the charter, even though the law would be permitted to stand.
The court’s decision was celebrated in Quebec, where the governing Parti Québécois has looked for wedges with the federal government and institutions like the supreme court.
The premier, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, had previously said his province’s right to decide its own laws was at risk.
Canada only recently fended off a threat to national unity after voters in Alberta rejected the initial stages of a separatist push. But Quebec’s newly elected government has shown an eagerness to clash with the prime minister, Mark Carney.
The supreme court’s judgment comes on the same day an appeal will be heard regarding a superior court decision that forces Quebec’s members of the national assembly to swear allegiance to King Charles to sit in the Salon Bleu – the chamber of the assembly. Lawmakers from a number of parties in the province recently refused to swear the oath of allegiance.

Lawsuit also alleging pressure on hardware suppliers comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching employees
OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the company of ⁠stealing its trade secrets ​and discouraging hardware suppliers from working on future OpenAI devices.
The suit, filed in northern California federal court, comes after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.
OpenAI filed the counterclaims ⁠in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple’s employment practices were designed to “trap” employees and prevent them from working on competitors’ technology.
OpenAI is developing AI-enabled personal electronic devices that threaten to “outcompete Apple on what ⁠Apple views as its own turf”, the company said in its Friday court filing.
OpenAI said in the filing that Apple ​gained confidential information by rehiring a former employee who worked ‌at OpenAI for six months. In ‌that time, the employee gained access to specific information on a new device as well as OpenAI’s roadmap for future hardware ‌products.
“Given the timing, it now appears that stealing those documents may have been his reason for joining OpenAI in the first place,” OpenAI said.
Apple denied using the rehired employee to access OpenAI’s confidential information and denied trying to suppress competition in AI device manufacturing.
“OpenAI’s counterclaims are a transparent attempt to distract from the substance of Apple’s lawsuit,” Apple said in a Friday statement.
Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for ‌talent and proprietary technology.
Apple sued OpenAI and the former Apple employees Tang Tan and Chang Liu in July, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner’s foray into consumer hardware.
Tan, ​a 24-year Apple employee who was a vice-president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch, was part of the group that launched the AI device startup io Products before it was acquired by OpenAI in 2025.
OpenAI and the employees have denied those allegations and said that Apple’s lawsuit depended on its unauthorized monitoring of Liu’s personal messages after he stopped working for Apple. OpenAI and ⁠attorneys for Tan and Liu did not immediately respond to a request for comment on ​Friday’s court filing.
In Friday’s filing, OpenAI criticized ​Apple for encouraging employees to do work on ​their personal Apple devices and accounts, then preventing those employees from an orderly separation of work and ​personal accounts when they leave ‌for new jobs.
OpenAI said ​that Apple continues to access ​former employees’ personal devices and accounts after they leave the company, enabling Apple to “monitor and ensnare departing employees” when they leave for competitors.
OpenAI said that 400 employees have left Apple for OpenAI so far, and Apple wants to intimidate other employees from leaving to find other tech companies.

Canada's top court has largely upheld a Quebec law banning public sector workers from wearing religious symbols, including the hijab and the cross.
The law, known as Bill 21, faced legal challenges from a range of groups, including female Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers, who argued it violated their fundamental rights.
Quebec passed the law in 2019 under a unique fixture of Canada's constitution called the "notwithstanding clause" - a legal loophole that allows governments to override certain rights, like freedom of religion.
The Supreme Court's decision is one of the most closely watched in Canadian history, with an impact that will be felt both in Quebec and across the country.
Reacting to the ruling on CBC, Prime Minister Mark Carney said his government would study its implications, adding it was important for all legislatures "to respect the rights and liberties of all Canadians, including those in the minority."
The Supreme Court was asked to weigh in on a number of questions, including on the constitutionality of Bill 21, whether Quebec's use of the notwithstanding clause was appropriate, and whether there are limits to its use.
On Friday, the top court confirmed the validity of Bill 21, but ruled that the law infringes on democratic rights by banning Quebec's elected officials from wearing a face covering for religious reasons.
The court also ruled that a Canadian court has the power to declare whether a law is consistent with the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms even if the notwithstanding clause is invoked, but that they would not do so in this case.
While the majority of the seven justices found that Quebec's law is largely valid, some dissented to parts of the decision.
Justices Andromache Karakatsanis, Michelle O'Bonsawin and Nicholas Kasirer wrote that the notwithstanding clause "cannot be used to authorize laws that are incompatible with the fundamental character of Canada as a free and democratic country".
Specifically, they said they believe the law infringes on the charter's guarantee to freedom of religion, freedom of expression and the right to equality.
What to know about the Supreme Court decision on Quebec's secularism bill
Civil liberty groups in Quebec have criticised Bill 21, saying it disproportionately affects Muslim women who wear the hijab, arguing that it has excluded them from key areas of public life in the province.
Stephen Brown, CEO of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, called the law "discriminatory" and criticised the court's decision.
"Entire categories of people are now barred from entire sectors of employment, not because of what they have done, but because of who they are," he said.
The chair of the English Montreal School Board, one of the main groups challenging the law, said the board was "obviously very disappointed" with the ruling.
"It wasn't the result we were looking for," Ortona told reporters. "But we do take solace from a lot of the declarations that were made by the court."
Quebec has argued that the law is necessary to uphold the province's state secularism - or laïcité - as a core component of its identity.
Earlier this year, the province passed another bill expanding its secularism rules to subsidised daycares and post-secondary institutions. It also restricted public prayer with fines for non-compliance.
The leader of the Bloc Québécois, a federal party that advocates for Quebec sovereignty, said Friday's ruling upheld the province's right to protect its values.
"We are now more than ever in a position to move forward with the preservation of the very elements that profoundly define the distinct nature of Quebec society," Yves-François Blanchet told reporters in French.

The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves
A court in Kenya has convicted the leader of a doomsday Christian cult of the manslaughter of 123 of his followers.
Paul Mackenzie was found guilty in Mombasa of ordering his followers, all adults, to fast to death in Shakahola forest near the coast between January 2021 and September 2023.
Earlier this month Mackenzie was jailed for 200 years for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children, in the same mass killing.
Mackenzie had pleaded not guilty to manslaughter and one of his lawyers said he would appeal against the conviction after sentencing, Reuters news agency reports.
Warning: This article contains details which some people might find distressing.
The court also convicted 29 others including Mackenzie's wife, Rhoda Mumbua Maweu, of their part in the manslaughter.
Sixty defendants were acquitted. The Director of Public Prosecutions indicated that an appeal would be launched against their acquittal.
The self-styled pastor was arrested in 2023 after the discovery of more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest, near the Indian Ocean coast.
The court found Mackenzie had "systematically persuaded his followers to fast until they died", Kenya's Office of The Director of Public Prosecutions said in a statement on Friday's verdict, which it described as "the final conviction" in the cases against him.
"Children were to go first, then women and then men, with Mackenzie himself meant to die last," the office said.
The prosecution argued that Mackenzie and his accomplices had acted together as part of a suicide pact to fast to death in order to "meet Jesus".
Witnesses testified that he had preached that education, medicine and ornaments were sinful.
Those who opposed his teachings were beaten to death, according to the verdict in his trial for the murder of 191 people.
The defendants had claimed that the victims had fasted out of their own free will.
assault causing actual bodily harm and five counts of cruelty to a child
being in possession of an article connected with an offence under Kenya's Prevention of Terrorism Act, 2012.
Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders
Mackenzie established Good News International Ministries in 2003. Over the next 16 years, the church grew in popularity to draw thousands of followers in branches across Kenya.
A television station called Times TV would broadcast his sermons from his church in the resort town of Malindi.
His End Days sermons included conspiracy theories that described education as "evil", healthcare as "against the doctrine" and digital identity cards as "the mark of the devil".
After the main church shut down in 2019, Mackenzie moved to Shakahola forest, encouraging his devotees to follow him.
The community was described as mud houses scattered across the vast forest.
"We lived a quiet normal life, fasting for a few days then having a small meal," said survivor Peter Shukrani, who was rescued after falling ill.
Stephen Mwiti, who lost six children to the cult, welcomed the conviction of Mackenzie for murder last month
When the shallow graves were discovered, local men were hired for the horrifying task of exhuming the remains.
"Every grave we found had at least three bodies," James, one of the gravediggers, told the BBC. "Some of the remains were of children as young as a few weeks old."
"We once found 12 bodies of children in a line inside a grave. It was massive, the bodies were arranged like clothes. One on top of another."
Gravediggers described some of the bodies of children as having had their "hands and legs tied and bodies wrapped in bedsheets".
Post-mortem records showed many of the victims had died of starvation while the remains of others were mostly skeletal, making the establishment of their cause of death impossible.
Stephen Mwiti, 48, said he had lost all six of his children to the cult. His former wife was one of those convicted of murder alongside Mackenzie.
"I'm a happy man, that all persons have been convicted," he told the BBC outside court last month.
"All six of my children died in Shakahola forest. I only found and buried the remains of my son Samuel."
The deaths have shone a spotlight on the lack of oversight of rogue religious activities and how they could have carried on for so long.
The gravity of the case prompted President William Ruto to set up a commission of inquiry, although this was later declared unconstitutional.

Both US coasts have been battered by severe Thanksgiving storms, leaving behind flooded roads, fallen trees, and widespread power outages for hundreds of thousands of people.

Beyond the travel disruption, impacts were widespread across the east Coast, and US President Donald Trump said he would consider releasing emergency funds.
