Manchester City 's leaky defence faces one of its most difficult tasks of the season with a trip to watertight Arsenal , aiming to put right their patchy recent form.
Enzo Maresca's side began the season with eight straight victories but have won only one of their past seven in all competitions inside 90 minutes and head to Emirates Stadium trailing the champions by six points even at this early juncture.
A Premier League defeat on Sunday could well have long-term consequences for City's title aspirations, with Mikel Arteta's men clearly standing above any other top-flight side as the ones to topple.
Though the Gunners dropped points last weekend with a draw at Newcastle , they continue to set the standards with a miserly defence that has conceded only seven goals in the club's opening 11 league games.
Asked why he felt City have dropped off in recent weeks, Maresca - who replaced Pep Guardiola as manager in the summer - said: "For me it's because we've had four months together. Transition requires time.
"It's probably because we won seven games in a row, with Champions League eight in a row. Everyone was thinking at City there's no transition but I've said many times I am not a magician. There is transition, it's normal.
"There are eight or nine new players, the manager is new so you need time and you can see different clubs when they had transition how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all."
'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt
"We are conceding too many goals and we need to avoid that," was an obvious statement made by Maresca following last Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham.
City followed that up with another home stalemate against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday and have now conceded in 10 successive games in all competitions for the first time in seven years.
"[It was] far, far too easy to play through [City]," said former England captain Alan Shearer of Rodrigo Muniz's goal for Fulham on Match of the Day.
" Fulham 's throw-in was level with their own 18-yard box. For them to get through is not acceptable at any level, let alone when you are playing for Manchester City and Muniz ran past the entire midfield [to score]."
City have managed only five clean sheets all campaign, which is in stark contrast to Arsenal , who have kept double the amount so far, while Newcastle 's opening goal ended a run off 445 minutes without the ball hitting their net.
Maresca's men also have an issue by conceding the opener, having done so seven times in the past 10 games, and of the 14 goals they have shipped, six have come inside the first 20 minutes.
An early Arsenal goal may well be an important factor in deciding Sunday's contest.
Asked how his side can improve defensively, Maresca said: "Video [analysis], meetings, [on] pitch coaching, It is a mix of that.
"Some of the goals we concede we can avoid, so hopefully we can do that."
Man City fan questions what's behind Marc Guehi's recent struggles
The injury to key defender William Saliba has almost gone unnoticed for Arsenal as Ezri Konsa has stepped in to fill the void at centre-back seamlessly since joining from Aston Villa in the summer.
The England international has established a formidable partnership with Gabriel and the two have quickly formed an impressive understanding this season.
Maresca, meanwhile, admitted he was still "trying to find different" solutions to his team, which has been highlighted by the chopping and changing of his backline.
In 16 Premier League and Champions League games this season, the Italian has used eight different combinations in defence, which has given players little chance of fostering any sort of on-pitch relationships with each other.
City have also made seven errors leading to goals, compared to Arsenal 's one.
"You are concerned in some way because that is a lot of errors leading to goals," said former City defender Nedum Onuoha. "With some of the best players you ask, 'what are they really good at?' For some it is the fact they don't make mistakes.
"They are ruthless and relentless in the way they play but at this moment in time City are being punished for those errors.
"A manager can have the tactics and do the team talks, but if people are going to continue to make those mistakes, they will suffer."
The chant of "1-0 to the Arsenal " has been synonymous with the Gunners over the years and it could not be more apt under Arteta.
Since the start of last season, his side have won 16 matches in all competitions by that particular scoreline, compared to six by City.
After beating Sunderland in a chaotic match in September, Maresca said he would "prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3", suggesting his side needed more control and he re-iterated that message after the Fulham draw.
"Sometimes you need to win games 1-0 for a small difference and to keep a clean sheet but in this moment we are not able to do that," he admitted.
City, though, have scored five more league goals than Arsenal in this campaign and Sunday's hosts have injury concerns over goalkeeper David Raya.
The Spaniard is a doubt with the shoulder problem he picked up at Newcastle , and compatriot Kepa Arrizabalaga may deputise again as he did in the 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday.
City have fond memories of coming up against Arsenal 's stand-in keeper, after Kepa's howler for the opening goal contributed to their 2-0 Carabao Cup final triumph back in March.
A repeat result on Sunday will provide a much-needed morale boost for Maresca and his team.

A sensational start for the Italian was swiftly followed by a dismal run and long faces in the team
This is the great known unknown in Manchester City’s run of one win – in addition to victory on penalties against Brighton in the Carabao Cup – in seven matches. After guilty verdicts were returned regarding the breaking of Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team went to Anfield and handed Liverpool a 3-0 schooling . Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory ( 3-2 over Ipswich , six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. City have appealed against the ruling, saying they are “innocent of the accusations”.
Nico O’Reilly’s stop-start season (four matches missed and three very short substitute appearances) has been a definite minus for the Maresca project because here is a muscular defender who offers pace, guile via a schemer’s ability to wander infield and unpick defences (he was a No 10 as a youth) and a goal threat. City conceded two in the first half without him in their 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest , before he came on. As a unit the defence is vulnerable, with Rúben Dias’s lack of pace and Marc Guéhi’s erratic displays key in the concerning leaking of goals.
Gianluigi Donnarumma has also been unreliable, with mistakes against Leipzig, Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain costing goals and points. The goalkeeper may also feel he should have stopped Rasmus Højlund’s opener in Tuesday’s 2-2 draw with Napoli . “I’m not worried about Gigio’s performance or form, knowing he has made some mistakes,” says Maresca, who has no credible competitor to the No 1 after James Trafford’s sale to Leeds in the last window. This points to a wider worry regarding questionable squad building that might not have occurred if Txiki Begiristain were still City’s director of football. His replacement, Hugo Viana, is not proving as shrewd in the market.
The Portuguese, who worked alongside Begiristain from April 2025, before taking over that summer, has made 18 signings: Enzo Fernández (£125m), Elliot Anderson (£116m), Ayyoub Bouaddi (£81.3m), Antoine Semenyo (£62.5m), Iliman Ndiaye (£60m), Tijjani Reijnders (£46.3m), Allan (£32m), Rayan Aït-Nouri (£31m), Rayan Cherki (£30.45m), Trafford (£27m), Donnarumma (£26m), Mathys Detourbet (£21.5m), Guéhi (£20m), Sverre Nypan (£12.5m), Jeremy Monga (£10m), Pierce Charles (£3m), Marcus Bettinelli (£2m), and Gerónimo Rulli (£1m). Before any add-ons, the cost is already more than an eye-watering £700m, yet, to date, only Anderson, Cherki and Ndiaye can be counted as unadulterated successes, with the form of Guéhi, Semenyo and Fernández dipping, and Bouaddi appearing promising. This leaves 10 players who have left, disappointed or must prove their potential, plus a back-up goalkeeper.
Maresca’s engine room has Anderson, a fine player but no Rodri (is anyone?), and Fernández, who is not a No 8, more a quasi-10 without Cherki’s sorcery in the position. Fernández’s role is akin to being Maresca’s on-field enforcer, the Italian having signed him from Chelsea after their time there together. Bouaddi, the main other midfielder, has impressed but is 19 so these are very early days for him, and with O’Reilly an auxiliary option and Mateo Kovacic seemingly in a bit-part role, City’s options hardly bulge. “We are trying different solutions,” Maresca says. “Last game [against Napoli] we started with Enzo, Ayyoub and Elliot. They were quite good, especially off the ball, and no doubt we’re going to find the right balance.”
Is the team totem and goal glutton happy? He was certainly glum post-Napoli, and has been spied gesticulating angrily during games. Maresca says: “Erling is a winner. It’s normal that he’s not happy when he’s not winning games but don’t forget a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch [after the Carabao Cup win against Brighton]. Erling is upset just like I am upset.” The question, though, is more of the existential kind regarding whether the Norwegian may debate a future away from City. Haaland signed a 10-year contract in January 2025 but this will mean zero should he wish to move on. If the appeal is lost and City are demoted a division (or worse), Haaland – and others – will surely depart.
All factors cited have to be nullified/solved by Maresca. Settling on a first XI while addressing a tactical blueprint that has a prevailing sluggishness with the odd flash of directness – Haaland’s winner in September against Coventry , for example, came via a quick Fernández pass to Semenyo, whose cross was converted – would help. On Friday Maresca offered a flat “no” when asked whether he may change his style. He also offered an explanation for the poor displays: “It’s easy to understand – because we are four months together. Transition requires time. Probably because we won eight games in a row [from the season’s start] people were thinking here there is no transition, but I’m not a magician. We have eight or nine new players, the manager is new – you need time. No panic at all. I understand we need to win games because it is a business.”

Report and free match highlights as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at The City Ground; Igor Jesus opened the scoring before Morgan Gibbs-White scored two. Emmanuel Emegha's brace in vain; Wesley Fofana was booed by the Chelsea supporters
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Morgan Gibbs-White scored two in Nottingham Forest’s 3-2 win over Chelsea at the City Ground as the crisis deepened for Xabi Alonso.
Igor Jesus volleyed Forest in front inside five minutes of what was a dismal first half for Chelsea and they never recovered parity. Wesley Fofana - booed by his own supporters throughout - conceded a penalty early in the second half that Gibbs-White converted.
Emmanuel Emegha did come off the bench to pull one back soon afterwards but another goal from the Forest captain better reflected the superiority of Oliver Glasner's side even if Emegha's second in the 89th minute made for a surprisingly nervy finale.
Forest began the evening beside the Trent with only goal difference keeping them out of the relegation zone, but victory lifts them clear of the bottom six. The spotlight now falls on Chelsea, who missed the chance to climb back into the top five.
It is four Premier League defeats in their last five games under Alonso who appears to be scrambling for solutions given the evidence of this team selection. It is not only Fofana under scrutiny at Chelsea. A club in disarray? Alonso needs to get a grip on it and fast.
Liam Delap had been the two-goal hero in the 3-1 win over Manchester City last time out at home and would have been desperate to score against another of his former clubs but it was Igor Jesus' stunning strike that silenced the Chelsea supporters early on.
"It is the first opportunity for them to play together, they have different strengths," Glasner had told Sky Sports beforehand. Igor Jesus' strengths include volleys beyond Emiliano Martinez, it turns out. It was his first goal at the City Ground since April.
Alonso had responded to the alarming defeat to Leeds by dropping Levi Colwill and playing Moises Caicedo in defence. The Chelsea boss changed to a back four as well in a bid to find some form after losing three of their previous four Premier League games.
"Today we need strong characters, big personalities," said Alonso beforehand. "Players that know what it takes to compete in the Premier League." That explained the decision to bring in Danny Welbeck up front, with Jordan Henderson holding midfield together.
But Welbeck was a passenger in the first half, having only seven touches of the ball - half as many as anyone else - while Henderson found himself overrun. Forest were at the back line time and again. Chelsea were fortunate to be only one down at the break.
Fofana had not endeared himself to supporters by giving an unauthorised interview in which he not only talked of being close to quitting football but appeared to joke about missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool. This performance was worse.
He was culpable for Forest's second goal, bested by Delap before hastily fouling him inside the penalty box in a rash attempt to recover. Gibbs-White slotted home from the spot and Fofana was substituted to the sound obscene chants from the Chelsea fans.
Alonso's side did pull one back through the young substitute Emegha, when Pedro Neto's shot was deflected kindly into his path. But Xaver Schlager's sumptuous ball clipped in behind the Chelsea defence allowed Gibbs-White to hook home his second.
Emegha nodded in another late on to make the decision to omit him after scoring the first goal against Leeds look even more of an error, but it was not enough to earn an undeserved point. Forest held on and are on the up again. Chelsea have problems.
Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner speaking in the press conference:
"It looks like we are progressing and this is what we all want to see. But also last time [against Man City] was the first swallow [that does not make a summer] and now it's the second swallow and I think everybody could feel it tonight.
"So stay humble, take this feeling of the win and the confidence and the belief but stay humble and prepare well for the three-game week before we face Brighton here.
"We are all feeling again that we are heading in the right direction. Still a lot to do, but every win helps in building confidence and trust. But still 12 points after 12 games is not enough."
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso speaking in the press conference:
"We are working, trying to find solutions, trying to do our best, but things are not going the way we want. And I don't understand any other way but to work, to try again.
"Because if we want to get something, it will have to come from us. No one will come from outside to give us a solution. And the quality that we need, the mentality that we need, it needs to come from within the team.
"Overall, we can do better. I think that we are going through a difficult moment of confidence, things are not clicking, things are not going the way we want.
"We know that in football, this can change quickly, or this can continue. So it's down to us to work and to find solutions to have a better feeling on the pitch and to get better results, because that's what we need."
Asked if he was frustrated with the Chelsea fans booing Wesley Fofana :
"We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need all the players, we need to stick together, because if not, it will get more complicated."

Renée Slegers has left her job as Arsenal Women’s head coach after a dismal set of results, with the club saying she has gone by mutual consent.
The 37-year-old had been under contract until 2029 after signing a three-and-a-half-year deal in January but six consecutive home draws in the Women’s Super League this season have left Arsenal sixth, 12 points behind the leaders, Chelsea, and eight points adrift of a European place.
Arsenal’s assistant coach Aaron D’Antino has also left, having been on the backroom staff since 2018. Arsenal’s director of women’s football, Clare Wheatley, told the club’s website a “change was necessary”, saying: “It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renée, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here.
“In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renée has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron. After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary.”
Arsenal’s chief executive, Richard Garlick, described Slegers as a “wonderful person” but said a new head coach was required to give the club the best chance of meeting the ambition “to compete for and win major trophies consistently”.
It is understood Arsenal were determined to give Slegers time and so stood by her earlier in the season when speculation about her future was mounting but that eventually the two parties concluded a change was needed.
Arsenal’s search to find Slegers’ replacement is under way but it is understood the club will not rush to make an appointment, because their priority is to find the best person rather than ensuring somebody is in place for their next match, at Everton on 11 December in the WSL.
Melissa Clarke-Reed, the former Brighton and London City Lionesses head coach, has been placed in interim charge. The club are believed to be comfortable with her, if necessary, overseeing the three games that precede the winter break. Arsenal then return to action on 10 January.
Slegers took charge in October 2024, initially as interim head coach, after the resignation of Jonas Eidevall, under whom she had worked as an assistant. She oversaw a run of 10 wins in 11 matches without defeat in caretaker charge, prompting the club to appoint her as the head coach on an 18-month deal.
The Dutchwoman then led Arsenal to one of the greatest moments in their history as they won the Women’s Champions League title on 24 May 2025, stunning Barcelona with a surprise 1-0 victory in Lisbon to land the club’s second European title and their first for 18 years.
The 2025-26 season ended with Arsenal second in the WSL, four points behind the champions, Manchester City. They were semi-finalists in the Champions League and League Cup and quarter-finalists in the FA Cup, but Slegers won – on home soil – the inaugural Fifa Women’s Champions Cup , a competition between the winners of the respective continental titles.
Arsenal had held high hopes of mounting a WSL title challenge this term, vying to win their first domestic league title since 2019, and had what appeared to be a strong summer transfer window, signing high-calibre internationals such as the England midfielder Georgia Stanway and the Spain full-back Ona Batlle.
They have had injuries, including to their integral midfielder Mariona Caldentey, who is sidelined with a hamstring problem. The team’s inability to break down opponents set up in a low block has been a repetitive issue, and on Sunday there were loud boos at the Emirates when they were held to a goalless draw by West Ham.
Slegers, a former Netherlands midfielder, managed the Swedish club Rosengård and Sweden’s under-23s before joining Arsenal in 2023 to work under Eidevall.

Renee Slegers initially joined Arsenal in 2023 as an assistant coach under Jonas Eidevall
Arsenal have parted company with head coach Renee Slegers by mutual consent after a disappointing start to the season.
Slegers, 37, was initially appointed on an interim basis in October 2024 before being handed the role permanently three months later.
The Dutchwoman led Arsenal to their second Women's Champions League title in May 2025 and the inaugural Fifa Women's Champions Cup in February 2026.
But she leaves with the team sixth in the Women's Super League after 11 matches - 12 points behind leaders Chelsea.
Assistant coach Aaron D'Antino has also left the club, with assistant Melissa Clarke-Reed placed in interim charge as they begin the search for a permanent replacement.
D'Antino had been part of Arsenal's coaching staff since August 2018.
Arsenal director of women's football Clare Wheatley said the decision had been "extremely difficult".
"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural Fifa Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron," she said.
"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."
Chief executive Richard Garlick paid tribute to both departing coaches, describing Slegers as "a wonderful person" who had played "an integral role in some of the most historic achievements in the club's history".
"Our ambition is to compete for and win major trophies consistently, and our recent results have led us to conclude that a change is necessary to give us the best opportunity to achieve those goals," he added.
Slegers' departure comes after weeks of pressure as Arsenal's WSL form continued to deteriorate.
While the Dutch coach delivered the Women's Champions League and Women's Champions Cup, results in the league have fallen below expectations this season.
Arsenal have endured a four-match winless run in the league and their struggles have been particularly stark at their own Emirates Stadium, where they have gone six matches without a victory.
For a side expected to challenge for major trophies every season, those dropped points are damaging as they have fallen well adrift of Chelsea and even eight points behind London City Lionesses, who are in the third Women's Champions League qualification spot.
A lack of goals has been central to Arsenal's struggles. They have scored just 11 times in 11 WSL matches this season - less than half the tally of Chelsea (29), second-placed Manchester City (28) and London City Lionesses (31).
Before Slegers' exit was confirmed on Friday, former Arsenal and England forward Lianne Sanderson had called for the manager to depart.
"I've been a big advocate for Renee to stay in the job, but after the Lyon game [a 2-0 home defeat in the Champions League], I felt this feeling in my stomach that it's time [to part ways]," Sanderson told FourFourTwo , external .
"That was probably the most defeated I have felt. The players weren't fighting, they had just shown nothing, there was no identity.
"The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results."
After Sunday's draw with West Ham, Slegers acknowledged performances and results had fallen short of expectations and made it clear she accepted responsibility.
"I love the club," she said. "We're going through a very, very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities, because the results haven't been good enough.
"In the second half we are chasing again, but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better.

Arsenal and Man City face off in the Premier League this weekend with the Gunners holding a six-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side; Mikel Arteta says the game is important for the title fight; watch Arsenal vs Man City live on Sky Sports this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Enzo Maresca said Premier League title rivals Manchester City and Arsenal couldn’t be compared after his side's early-season form raised expectations.
Maresca described Sunday's fixture, live on Sky Sports , as "four months vs seven years", referencing the transition City are going through following Pep Guardiola's departure and the longevity of head coach Mikel Arteta at Arsenal.
"We have been top of the league for two and a half months until November 1. Now we are not there and everyone is comparing," said Maresca.
"For me, it's seven years together against four months together so you cannot compare. I understand everyone is trying to do that, but from my point of view everything is clear."
City have fallen six points behind Arsenal after failing to win in their last four league games while they've only won two of their last seven in all competitions.
"It's more than easy to understand why because we've had four months together," said Maresca when addressing his side's form.
"Transition requires time. Probably because we won seven games in a row, eight with the Champions League, everyone was thinking that there was no transition.
"I said many times, I'm not a magician. There's a transition, it's normal. We have eight or nine new players, the manager is new, so you need time.
"You can see with different clubs when they transition, how complicated it is. For me, it's completely normal.
"I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all, understanding that we need to win games because it's our business. For me, it's all normal."
In midweek, Erling Haaland made some concerning comments, claiming that "you have to question everything" after their draw against Napoli in the Champions League. But Maresca insists there is no issue with the striker.
"It's normal that results affect the mood, that's why we need to win games," said Maresca. "I don't see any problem with Erling."
"Erling is a winner. It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games. Not just Erling, everyone. Don't forget, three weeks ago, he was dancing on the pitch."
Maresca is prioritising the long-term vision he has for City. "The present is important but the future is much more important in terms of improving and building something with the team.
"Where we can be on Sunday night if we win, lose or draw, it's important but it's a long season. We'll see where we are in February and March and from there you can set the goals.
"Now, I think it's useless speaking about targets or where we can be at the end of the season."
But facing champions Arsenal on Sunday will give them idea of their progress.
"You need to show personality," he said. "That's why it's also a nice game for us to see where we are in terms of personality and from there try to understand the situation."
In the red corner, Arsenal manager Arteta knows how important matches are against their rivals in their bid to retain the Premier League title for the first time.
"When we played the home games against big teams, that becomes crucial in the title challenge," he said. "We know how important the home games are to make the difference.
"But we're in November, we know how long we have to play. But that's for every single team."
Asked whether City's form has anything to do with the club being found guilty of 115 serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in September, Arteta admitted that "it's a question for City."
He then went on to say: "All I can say is when I watch them play is a lot of games that they have done more merits than the opponent, but this is football. To win games, that's merit to the way they play."
Asked if City are Arsenal's closest challengers for the title, Arteta replied: "We don't know, I think the challenge is for us, and the opportunity is for us.
"We cannot control what the opponents are going to do; we just need to give ourselves the best version, and I'm sure the atmosphere is going to be incredible on Sunday, and we need to enjoy and embrace those kinds of games and go for it."
Arteta did not, however, want to be drawn on the atmosphere the Emirates Stadium could produce in the wake of City's guilty verdict. The club deny all the charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict. No sanctions have yet been announced.
On the pitch, Arsenal are sweating on the fitness of goalkeeper David Raya while centre-back William Saliba will have to wait patiently to work his way back into the side following injury.
For City, the game comes too soon for winger Antoine Semenyo, who could return next week.

Manchester United have triggered their one-year option on captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.
The 32-year-old's deal was due to expire next summer but sources say both parties decided it was in their best interests to activate the option through to 2028.
It means overseas clubs will not be able to approach Fernandes when the transfer window opens on 1 January.
The Portugal international confirmed on Tuesday that discussions over a new contract had been paused. Sources say they will resume once United's league position has improved.
Fernandes has made 343 appearances for United, scoring 115 goals, since his £47m move from Sporting in January 2020.
Last season he broke the Premier League assists record and scooped all of the individual player of the year awards after an outstanding campaign as United finished third.
While there is doubt over his long-term future, extending the contract means United would be able to command a fee for Fernandes should he leave in the summer.
United had been open to selling Fernandes in the summer of 2025, with Saudi Pro-League club Al Hilal offering a huge deal.
After discussing the situation with his wife, Fernandes decided to stay, though he later said it "hurt" United were willing to sell him. He reiterated on Tuesday he was still ambitious to win the biggest honours in the game.
Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's Premier League encounter with Brentford after returning from the Champions League trip to Sporting with a virus.
The playmaker, who scored both goals in the 2-2 draw with his former club, but did not train on Friday and head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he would take a decision on his captain's fitness on Saturday morning.
"We are going to assess during the day and then tomorrow see how he is when he wakes up," said Pochettino. "We are not going to take any risks."
Pochettino is preparing for his first home game as Man Utd boss
Pochettino was criticised by former Liverpool and England midfielder Jamie Redknapp on the Overlap earlier this week.
Reference was made to the former Tottenham, Paris St-Germain and Chelsea coach high-fiving Sky Sports reporter Patrick Davidson after his side's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, as evidence Pochettino had lost his edge.
"When I saw Pochettino at Southampton and I saw him at Tottenham, he looked like he had that Argentinian dog in him," said Redknapp.
"I look at him now and he's high-fiving everyone, he's got the bracelets on, he's got the barnet. I think he's gone too nice."
It seems someone had mentioned the observation to Pochettino as he went off on a tangent at his Friday news conference when asked about a "crazy" first week that included red cards, refereeing errors, disallowed goals and a drone filming training.
"What are we going to do? Start to cry?" he asked. "No. We have to be strong, believe and keep going. I cannot judge the past. Who am I to do that? I was in Cincinnati. I was outside. I need to shut my mouth, say nothing and start from now.
"Sometimes we are so confusing two words that means something similar; nice and good. I am not nice. We have to be good. It is a different thing. We know when we need to push, when we need to be strong, and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything.
Pochettino also confirmed £70m midfielder Carlos Baleba is expected to be out until the last week in January with the hamstring injury he sustained against Roma on 3 November.
Forward Marcus Rashford had begun to do individual work outside as he tries to recover from a hip problem that has kept him out since 13 October.

Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes.
Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers.
Immediate focus is on improving results, with United second-bottom of the Premier League with one win and also 19th in the Champions League standings. Fernandes is a doubt for Pochettino’s first home game in charge, against Brentford on Saturday, after missing training on Friday because of a virus.
Pochettino lost 4-0 at Liverpool in his first league game and followed that with a 2-2 draw at Sporting in the Champions League. He is confident of transforming the club and made clear he would not take a softly-softly approach. Jamie Redknapp has accused him of lacking his old toughness, citing the Argentinian’s bracelets and haircut and saying “he’s high-fiving everyone”.
“I am not nice,” Pochettino said. “I am trying to be good. But be careful, because we know when we need to push, when we need to be strong and when we need to build something to improve the atmosphere and relationship and everything. We have our experience and we are going to try to give everything to put the team, the club, the players on track again. And we really believe, we really believe that we can do it. It’s only a matter of time.”
If United beat Brentford it would be a first domestic win in 90 days. The performance against Sporting gave a vision of Pochettino’s plan to be aggressive and press high. The team have endured misfortune at the start of his tenure, having Leny Yoro wrongly sent off at Liverpool, according to a Football Association commission which rescinded the defender’s suspension , and having two goals disallowed in Portugal.
“We need to accept that,” Pochettino said. “What are we going to do? Start to cry? No. Be strong, believe, keep going. I can think of many positive things in the two games. Maybe we didn’t win but for sure I think we are building our journey and for sure in the last seven, eight days we found a group of players, a group of staff, that want to help and want to be there, to help the team to perform and win games.”
Pochettino will be without the midfielder Carlos Baleba until late January but Marcus Rashford returned to individual training on Friday.

Renee Slegers leaves Arsenal after less than two years in charge; Slegers led Gunners to Women's Champions League title in May 2025, but exits after poor start to 2026/27 campaign; the Gunners sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off the top and have not won at home in the league all season
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Renee Slegers has been sacked as Arsenal head coach after a poor start to the Women's Super League season.
Slegers led Arsenal to Women's Champions League glory in May 2025 , having initially stepped up from assistant to Jonas Eidevall on an interim basis, then narrowly missed out on the WSL title to Manchester City in 2025/26.
Such was her success at the time, the Dutchwoman signed a new contract with the club in January 2026, running until 2029.
But a poor start to the 2026/27 campaign, in which Arsenal went on a five-game winless run in the WSL for the first time in their history, has culminated in Slegers' departure just 10 months into her new deal.
The Gunners remain winless at home in the WSL this season having drawn a sixth consecutive game against West Ham on Sunday.
Arsenal sit sixth in the WSL, 12 points off leaders Chelsea and eight points behind London City Lionesses in the third and final Champions League position.
Slegers' side have also only scored 11 goals in 11 WSL matches this season - only Everton and bottom club Charlton have managed fewer this term.
Her assistant coach Aaron D'Antino - who has been with the Gunners since 2018 - also leaves the club, with former Brighton boss and current Arsenal head of analytics Melissa Clarke-Reed taking interim charge.
"It was an extremely difficult decision to part ways with Renee, who has led the team with dedication and commitment throughout her time here," said director of women's football Clare Wheatley.
"In leading us to glory in the Champions League and the inaugural FIFA Champions Cup, Renee has made a significant and lasting contribution to the history of Arsenal Football Club, with close support from Aaron.
"After careful reflection, it is clear that results have been below the expected level, and change is necessary."
Analysis from Sky Sports News' Anton Toloui : "It's been described to me as a sad day at Arsenal. The club did not want to have to make this decision, but results this season have dictated Renee Slegers' future, and they have had to make the difficult choice to let her go.
"Richard Garlick, the club's CEO, informed staff just before 3pm, and director of football Claire Wheatley has been ringing round the players, most of whom are on international duty, to let them know that Slegers won't be there when they come back to the club.
"It's a difficult time. They went into the season as narrow favourites to end their title WSL drought - they haven't won the competition since 2019. But this season, the results have not lived up to the hype, despite the fact they went on a big summer recruitment drive, bringing in the likes of Georgia Stanway, Misa Rodriguez, and Ona Batlle.
"Arsenal currently sit sixth in the table, six draws from six home games in the league so far. Only three wins in the competition sees them way off the title hunt, maybe even outsiders to make it into the Champions League this season.
"But Slegers leaves the club with a lot of love after taking over from Jonas Eidevall, lifting up the spirits and bringing the club their first Champions League trophy for 18 years."
Analysis from Sky Sports News' Uma Gurav: "It was one of those decisions that felt like it was coming, particularly after the last set of games that Arsenal have played.
"This follows Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham at the Emirates last weekend and what's so significant about that is it means Arsenal are yet to win at home in the WSL this season, a place that used to be their fortress.
"Now, it's a place where so many teams have come and taken points off them.
"It just didn't look like a coherent Arsenal team on Sunday. Players were coming off in tears and it means they have a lot of work to do to get anything out of this season.
"At the moment, they are eight points off those Champions League places. They wanted to win the WSL this season - that hasn't happened and I think that's partly why this decision has been taken.
"Arsenal have got three more games before Christmas, all away games at Everton and Charlton in the WSL and then one against Inter Milan to see what they can salvage so far from this block of games.
"When we return from the international break, it will be a new Arsenal, with a new team in charge. Let's see if they can turn their season around."

Bruno Fernandes' contract was expiring at the end of this season but it will now run until the summer of 2028; the Man Utd captain and the club are in agreement that it makes sense to return to negotiations in the future, with full focus on improving the club's current position
Manchester United have triggered their 12-month option to extend captain Bruno Fernandes' contract.
His deal was previously set to expire at the end of this season but will now run until summer 2028.
United have been in talks with Fernandes over extending his contract since the summer.
Sky Sports News understands both parties are in agreement that it makes sense to return to negotiations in the future - with full focus on improving the club's current position.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Triggering the club option now is logical from United's perspective, as clubs could have approached Fernandes over a pre-contract agreement in January. This contract clause activation prevents that.
Meanwhile, Fernandes was absent from United training on Friday - ahead of their game against Brentford on Saturday - due to illness.
Fernandes is understood to be under the weather and is being kept away from the squad ahead of the Brentford game.
On whether he'll make the game, Mauricio Pochettino said: "We don't know. He got a virus in Portugal. He finished the game with a problem and today he cannot be part of the training session.
"We'll see. We are going to see during the day, and [Saturday], how he wakes up. We are not going to take any risks."
"What triggering this option does is reduce the chance to zero that any club outside of the Premier League can approach Fernandes from Europe's top leagues around a potential move next summer for free.
"So this move protects both the club and the player from that situation.
"We know he's been the subject of interest in the last few summers, especially from Saudi Arabia.
"I think negotiations will continue in the future over Fernandes' long-term future, but for now he will remain at the club until the summer of 2028."
"They are protecting their asset. It is as simple as that. They are not in a position to fall out with their best player.
"They need him to go and perform to make sure they do not go down. I do not think they are in a relegation fight; they have the manager who will sort a lot of things out.
"Right now, they are a team devoid of all confidence. They could lose to Brentford, but I do not think they are in a relegation fight. They will end up finishing in mid-table.
"They have some very average players, hence the position, but they needed to trigger the clause to protect the asset and then get the money in the summer, if they have to."
Last week, Fernandes exclusively told Sky Sports that United have offered him a new contract - but he has put discussions on hold as he insists the club's priority must be returning to winning ways.
Fernandes has rejected two contract offers from United . The club's initial proposal was made in the summer when discussions first began over a new deal, but was turned down by the Portuguese, who signed his last contract in August 2024.
The United captain said: "I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.
"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.
"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on.
"I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.
"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract.
"But about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to one side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games.
"My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am."
Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada also spoke to Sky Sports last week about Fernandes' contract talks and said: "Listen, I've said before, we have a tremendous amount of respect for Bruno. We're very fortunate to have him as a captain.
"What he's done for this team over the last six, seven years is absolutely incredible. Last year he won, I think, all the individual awards you can win.
"And we're very proud to have him as captain. It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private. I think it's something that needs to be discussed behind the scenes between him and the club."

When asked whether he had any regrets about running the length of the pitch to goad the Middlesbrough supporters he used to call his own with a mock crying celebration, Finn Azaz was unequivocal. “None whatsoever,” said the Southampton playmaker. And you get the sense that very few associated with his club disagreed.
Southampton, and their manager Tonda Eckert, long ago admitted their Spygate crime. Based on the behaviour of many connected to the south-coast club – their manager a notable exception – they have embraced it. The sense of aggrievement that it cost them the chance of promotion last season remains.
So when the former Boro player Azaz sealed victory in a most heated of contests – the first time these two clubs had met since the scandal – adding a second goal to Ryan Manning’s opener, it was like a champagne cork had been popped. “They sang about my family home and away last season so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back,” said Azaz.
It was an astonishing end to a new rivalry that will doubtless only grow given the continued brazen conduct of the guilty party. In the buildup to the match, there had been a public desire from both managers to move on from the events of last May: the intern caught snooping on Middlesbrough training, Southampton’s subsequent expulsion from the Championship playoff final despite claiming victory on the pitch, and the five-month saga spent meting out full punishments.
So it was eye-catching, to say the least, when Southampton – and you would have to assume, given the importance of the subject matter, those at the very top – signed off the release of an extraordinary video uploaded on to social media on Friday morning and then replayed pre-match on the big screens.
The clip, voiced by a local content creator, featured footage from both playoff semi-final legs, emphasising Southampton’s highs – “the night was ours” – and the lows – “until it wasn’t” – while carefully avoiding any specific reference to Spygate itself. It also, pointedly, showed Oli McBurnie wheeling away in celebration at Wembley after scoring the stoppage-time goal that sent Hull , and not Middlesbrough, to the Premier League. And it then, with a total absence of self-awareness, 55 seconds into a backwards-looking 79-second video, delivered the farcical line: “People talk about last season. But we’re focused on this one.”
Many at Southampton have clearly neither forgiven nor forgotten, as was evident in the playing of Oasis’s Stop Crying Your Heart Out at the final whistle. A box of tissues had even been placed in front of the managers for the post-match press conference, which a shocked Eckert removed as soon as it was pointed out.
“I didn’t like the video,” he said. “If we look back a couple of months, the reality is both clubs have lost – one off the pitch and the other on the pitch. It’s an episode, I think, that is good to close for both clubs and to move forward. I think it’s been one of the best games that the Championship can offer. I hope these games are remembered for the football and not what happens around it. I hope that everyone knows these things don’t come from me.” Of Azaz’s celebration, he simply said: “I’ll talk to him.”
The atmosphere at St Mary’s was febrile as both sets of supporters ran through their repertoire – the away fans describing Southampton as “cheating bastards” and the hosts responding by suggesting “we’ll spy when we want”. The match was enthralling, with chances aplenty and tension that rose until a melee-filled finale that produced 10 yellow cards.
Manning broke the deadlock on 59 minutes when an excellent referee’s advantage culminated in James Bree drilling the ball across the box for him to poke home. A terrible defensive error then presented Azaz with the ball inside the Boro penalty area, and he slotted it in before embarking on his pitch-long celebratory venture. It was easy to forget the context – that Middlesbrough remain top of the table, but Southampton would be above them without their four-point deduction.
“I can understand emotions happen, but it’s important to draw a line under it,” said Kim Hellberg, Boro’s manager, calmly. “It’s tough trying to keep the class in those moments.”
The managers are doing all they can to make it so. Everyone else, not so much. But it makes for some spectacle.

Alexander Kartveli Batum Uluslararası Havalimanı'ndan olumsuz hava koşulları ve şiddetli rüzgar nedeniyle yaklaşık 2,5 saat gecikmeli olarak kalkış yapan kafile, yaklaşık 1,5 saatlik uçuşun ardından İstanbul'a vardı.
Sabiha Gökçen Havalimanı Genel Havacılık Terminali'ne iniş yapan Beşiktaş'ı siyah-beyazlı taraftarların yanı sıra çok sayıda basın mensubu karşıladı.
Burada açıklamada bulunan takım kaptanı Orkun Kökçü, "Yoğun duygular yaşadım, penaltı kaçırdım. Sorumluluk duygusu nedeniyle biraz kendime fazla yüklendim ama gol attığım için mutluyum. Takım arkadaşlarıma teşekkür etmek istiyorum. 'Orada maçı kazanabilecek miyiz?' korkusu vardı. Takım olarak kazandık. Bizi yoran şeyler yaşadık takım ve aile olduğumuzu gösterdik. Böyle devam etmek istiyoruz." diye konuştu.
Taraftarların yanında olduklarını aktaran Orkun, şunları kaydetti:
“Polis öyle bir güç kullanıyorsa taraftar kendini korumak için öyle bir şey yapmıştır. Biz taraftarımızın arkasındayız. Soruşturmayı yapsınlar, sonuçlarına da katlanırız. Hiçbir sıkıntı yok. Ülkemiz çok güzel bir destek verdi, bize iyi hissettirdi. Tüm Türkiye arkamızdaydı, herkesin desteğini hissettik. Herkese teşekkür etmek istiyorum, bizim için milli bir meseleydi.”
Beşiktaş Futbol Direktörü Önder Özen, tüm Türkiye'nin manevi gücünü hissettiklerini dile getirdi.
Emeği geçen herkese teşekkür eden Özen, "Sağ salim döndük. Zorlu bir seyahat oldu, hem gidiş hem dönüş. Maçın bir bölümü oynanmadı, sonra durum toparlandı. Emeği geçen herkese teşekkür ederiz. Türkiye'den büyük bir ilgi oldu. Hem devlet katında hem yurttaşlar büyük destek verdiler. Onların manevi gücünü oyuncularım hissetti. Camia adına herkese teşekkür ederiz. Sizler de yaşananları objektif şekilde çok güzel aktardınız." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.
Soruşturmaya ilişkin soru üzerine ise Özen, şöyle devam etti:
"Bizim elde ettiğimiz tüm doküman ve görüntüleri ilettik, toparladık. Bizim hukuk kurulu değerlendirmeye aldı. Sahadaki UEFA yetkilileriyle görüşmelerimizi yaptık, çok büyük bir şey beklemiyoruz. Aşağı yukarı ne olacağını biliyoruz ama seslendirmek istemiyoruz. Bunu hukuk kurulundaki arkadaşlarımız söylerse daha doğru olur. Önemli bir sorun yaşayacağımızı düşünmüyorum çünkü orantısız güç kullanılan taraf bizim taraftarlarımız oldu. Orada mağduriyeti yaşayan taraf ev sahibi olmamıza rağmen bizim tarafımız oldu."
Özen, Galatasaray derbisi için bir erteleme talep etmeyeceklerini de vurgulayarak sözlerini şöyle tamamladı:
"Emniyet müdürü sağ olsun çok yardımcı oldu ama geri kalan yerel makamlardan yeteri kadar destek alamamış olduğumuzu söylememiz gerekiyor. İstanbul'dan gelen emniyetçi arkadaşlarımız oldu, spor polisine teşekkür ederiz. Onlar da çok destek oldu. Sağ olsunlar, var olsunlar. Erteleme konusu daha önce konuştuk, bahane yok devam. Aynen olduğu gibi ve sizlerin gözlemlediği gibi yorumluyorum. Kimse bahanenin arkasına saklanmadı, cesareti, yüreklerini ortaya koydular. Ülkeyi de kulübü de çok iyi temsil ettiler. Hepsinin ayaklarına sağlık."
Sabiha Gökçen Havalimanı meydan otoritesi Havaalanı İşletme ve Havacılık Endüstrileri AŞ'den (HEAŞ) yapılan açıklamaya göre, siyah-beyazlı kafile için özel karşılama töreni düzenlendi.
Havalimanındaki özel karşılama töreni, dün akşam oynanan karşılaşmada siyah-beyazlı taraftarların Filistin'e destek amacıyla açtığı pankartın ardından, Gürcistan polisinin tribünlere sert müdahalede bulunması üzerine Beşiktaş camiasıyla dayanışma amacıyla organize edildi.
Batum'dan havalanan Beşiktaş kafilesini taşıyan uçak, İstanbul Sabiha Gökçen Uluslararası Havalimanı'na inişinin ardından, HEAŞ bünyesindeki Havalimanı Kurtarma ve Yangınla Mücadele (ARFF) ekiplerince apronda oluşturulan su takının altından geçerek park pozisyonuna yanaştı.
HEAŞ tarafından gerçekleştirilen karşılamayla, deplasmandan dönen siyah-beyazlı kafileye "hoş geldiniz" mesajı iletilirken, takım ayrımı gözetmeksizin Beşiktaş camiasıyla birlik ve dayanışma vurgusu yapıldı.

Renee Slegers has left Arsenal after two years in charge; for a tenure that started so spectacularly, things have gone sour at a rapid rate; Sky Sports' Laura Hunter analyses how did the Dutchwomen's position became untenable
Arsenal have parted company with Renee Slegers after less than two years permanently in charge, during which time the club celebrated unrivalled highs and endured dispiriting lows. The polarisation of the Dutchwoman's tenure is quite unusual.
Slegers' impact was instantaneous when she assumed control of Arsenal back in October 2024, initially on an interim basis. Stepping up to take over from Jonas Eidevall, previously his assistant, was seamless. She already knew the squad. The squad were just as familiar with her. The fit was perfect.
Slegers took a side on the slide to the zenith of the women's game within seven months. Beating Barcelona on a barmy night in Lisbon to lift the Champions League trophy, the only English club ever to do so, was a triumph few would have considered possible when she took the role. Slegers described it as "above all expectations".
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
The root of her success was an open secret. Calm and composed but equally candid, Slegers' authority was built on a transparency that previously never existed. There was trust, accountability and mutual respect. As a collective, Arsenal's bond was their greatest asset.
Arsenal's squad was once filled with stalwarts of the game. Some still remain, but the nucleus of the group has begun to move towards a younger, more dynamic composition. There is a lot of talent.
But perhaps Arsenal lost a bit of personality when they allowed both Katie McCabe and Beth Mead to leave in the same summer - to join direct WSL rivals. Those decisions were footballing ones, and yet, it feels like the soul of the club, those who understand and embody what it is to be Arsenal, is lacking.
They also let Victoria Pelova move across north London to Spurs, only to emerge as one of the league's top scorers. The 27-year-old, at peak age, has a better goals per 90 ratio than any Arsenal player this term - including Alessia Russo - and the best striking accuracy of any midfielder in the division.
With the benefit of hindsight, it's difficult to view any of those outgoings as helpful to Arsenal's cause.
Slegers has failed to find a balanced formula this season, criticised for using key players in unfamiliar positions. Right-back Ona Batlle has spent all campaign at left-back. Russo has played nearly 40 per cent of her total league minutes as a No 10.
The composition of the back four changes every game. Leah Williamson has had three different centre-back partners, none of which have stuck. And the full-back positions rotate weekly. In total, Slegers has fielded six different defensive arrangements across 11 games.
Her total starting XI changes amount to 29, which is not unusual given the size of Arsenal's squad. Chelsea have made 31. But a lack of consistency is not helping a team under pressure. Nor have in-game tactical adjustments been able to flip a result frequently enough.
Olivia Smith is the only player to have scored a goal as a substitute all season, rescuing a draw against newly-promoted Birmingham in October. Such limited impact from a squad of Arsenal's size reflects most damningly on those in charge of its deployment.
It is no secret that Arsenal cannot break down a compact defence. It's been a systematic failing that pre-dates Slegers - but has worsened. Opposition teams travel to the Emirates and set up for a point, almost always leaving with one.
Arsenal have no problem establishing territorial dominance because the squad is filled with ball-players but once in the final third, a lack of penetration means they struggle to manipulate deep defensive shapes. Possession ends with a predictable cross or a shot into traffic.
Russo's threat remains but she has no creative support. She is Plan A, B and C. That tactical inertia is harming Arsenal's chances of winning games, especially at the Emirates, where expectant home crowds demand more than six consecutive draws containing a frugal four goals.
Arsenal's conversion rate from chances created and shots on target is at an all-time low. Their latest goalless stalemate with West Ham saw their conversion percentage at home plummet to just 2.8. More than a problem, it's a pattern.
An atmosphere that was once the great envy of the league has gone stale. Perhaps that is the clearest symptom of Slegers' stagnation.
Last season Arsenal won eight of their 11 home games. Slegers actually maintained an unbeaten record in the league at home, but drawing all six Emirates outings this year led fans to turn sour - or not turn up at all. Attendances are down and the shift in mood is hardly subtle.
There is no vibe to Arsenal in this context. Hoping they eventually revert to type no longer feels sufficient given how much evidence there is to the contrary. Every home performance is a repeat of the one that went before it: forced and faceless. Main character energy has long faded.
Six home draws cannot be considered freak variance. It's a cycle opposition teams have learned to use against them.
A final nail in the coffin concerns how far Arsenal have fallen away from challenging for domestic honours. Spurs are five points better off in the position ahead. Man City are 10 clear. And the gap to leaders Chelsea is 12.
Arsenal had a foundation from which to build after a European triumph no one planned or expected. It was a gift. But the club have allowed that momentum to fizzle into nothingness.
This is a team in decline; a change of leaders was unavoidable.
Analysis from Sky Sports News' Anton Toloui : "It's been described to me as a sad day at Arsenal. The club did not want to have to make this decision, but results this season have dictated Renee Slegers' future, and they have had to make the difficult choice to let her go.
"Richard Garlick, the club's CEO, informed staff just before 3pm, and director of football Claire Wheatley has been ringing round the players, most of whom are on international duty, to let them know that Slegers won't be there when they come back to the club.
"It's a difficult time. They went into the season as narrow favourites to end their title WSL drought - they haven't won the competition since 2019. But this season, the results have not lived up to the hype, despite the fact they went on a big summer recruitment drive, bringing in the likes of Georgia Stanway, Misa Rodriguez, and Ona Batlle.
"Arsenal currently sit sixth in the table, six draws from six home games in the league so far. Only three wins in the competition sees them way off the title hunt, maybe even outsiders to make it into the Champions League this season.
"But Slegers leaves the club with a lot of love after taking over from Jonas Eidevall, lifting up the spirits and bringing the club their first Champions League trophy for 18 years."
